title: India ITME 2026: How Barmag is reshaping the Future of Man-Made Fiber Production
title_ko: 인도 ITME 2026: Barmag가 인공 섬유 생산의 미래를 재편하는 방법
summary: The textile industry is entering a groundbreaking era. Manufacturers face rising energy prices, growing sustainability demands, increasing labor shortages, and an unprecedented need for flexibility. For a globally active textile… The post India ITME 2026: How Barmag is reshaping the Future of Man-Made Fiber Production appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: The textile industry is entering a groundbreaking era. Manufacturers face rising energy prices, growing sustainability demands, increasing labor shortages, and an unprecedented need for flexibility. For a globally active textile industry, where competitiveness is closely linked to production efficiency and cost leadership, this means that technology is no longer merely a means of improving operational processes – it is increasingly becoming a strategic differentiator. Against this backdrop, Barmag will present a innovation portfolio at India ITME that goes far beyond incremental machine upgrades. From December 4 to 9, 2026, Barmag’s experts will be presenting next-generation spinning concepts, smart factory platforms, and groundbreaking technologies for filament, staple fibers and nonwovens at their booth C15 in Hall 10 at India Expo Centre & Mart in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India. In doing so, the company is laying the foundation for what it calls “A New Era” of textile production. At the center of this transformation stands one development in particular: Barmag POY 2.0. André Wissenberg, Head of Marketing, Corporate Communications and Public Affairs at Barmag Every few years, an innovation emerges that fundamentally changes how an industry thinks about production. Barmag believes POY 2.0 represents exactly such a moment. The new spinning concept is the result of a complete re-evaluation of the entire POY process chain, from spinning and quenching to winding, parallel with a digital process control. Rather than improving isolated components, engineers reimagined the interaction between all process steps. summary: Ambassador Md. Daud Ali inaugurated the Bangladesh Pavilion at “Fashion World Tokyo (Autumn) 2026” at Tokyo Big Sight today by cutting a ribbon and visited the stalls. He praised the high quality of the Bangladeshi products on display and interacted with the participating entrepreneurs. A total of 25 Bangladeshi companies with 27 booths under the […] The post Bangladesh Pavilion at “Fashion World Tokyo (Autumn) 2026” appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Ambassador Md. Daud Ali inaugurated the Bangladesh Pavilion at “Fashion World Tokyo (Autumn) 2026” at Tokyo Big Sight today by cutting a ribbon and visited the stalls. He praised the high quality of the Bangladeshi products on display and interacted with the participating entrepreneurs. A total of 25 Bangladeshi companies with 27 booths under the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB), along with 5 other renowned institutions, are participating in the fair. Following the inauguration, a seminar titled “Bangladesh: Sourcing Excellence for Apparel, Home Textile and Leather Products” was held at the exhibition hall of Tokyo Big Sight. Jointly organized by the Embassy of Bangladesh in Tokyo, EPB, and the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO), the seminar brought together business representatives and investors from both countries. Addressing the seminar as the chief guest, Ambassador Md. Daud Ali stated that Bangladesh is not merely a manufacturing country, but a reliable sourcing and investment partner for Japanese businesses. He highlighted the immense potential of Bangladesh’s robust production base across various sectors, including apparel, textiles, leather and footwear, pharmaceuticals, ceramics, agro-processing, and ITES. He further expressed optimism that the Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) will further strengthen bilateral trade and economic cooperation between the two nations. Mr. Yuji Ando, Senior Director for Global Strategy at JETRO, delivered a presentation highlighting the quality and competitive, reasonable pricing of Bangladesh’s apparel, home textiles, and leather products. Sans will operate alongside Spinnere as a sister company within Reshoring Textiles, and industry veteran John Garner has been named its CEO. Robert Antoshak has been named Chief Marketing […]
content: STONEVILLE, N.C. — October 8, 2026 — Reshoring Textiles has acquired Sans Technical Fibers, an American producer of high tenacity LDI nylon 6.6 and polyester yarns. Robert Antoshak has been named Chief Marketing Officer of Reshoring Textiles. title: Global textiles industry remains under pressure
summary: The global textile industry continues to face challenging business conditions despite a modest improvement in sentiment, according to the latest Global Textile Industry Survey (GTIS) published by the International Textile Manufacturers Federation (ITMF). The 40th survey, conducted between 21 and 29 September 2026, shows that the global business situation improved slightly to -23 percentage points, […] The post Global textiles industry remains under pressure appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: The global textile industry continues to face challenging business conditions despite a modest improvement in sentiment, according to the latest Global Textile Industry Survey (GTIS) published by the International Textile Manufacturers Federation (ITMF). The 40th survey, conducted between 21 and 29 September 2026, shows that the global business situation improved slightly to -23 percentage points, significantly above the record low of -46 percentage points recorded in November 2023. However, the industry remains under pressure amid persistent uncertainty, weak demand and rising production costs. Regional differences remain pronounced. South Asia (+13 percentage points) and Africa (+9 percentage points) are the only regions reporting positive business conditions. Europe (-36 percentage points), South America (-44 percentage points) and North and Central America (-56 percentage points) continue to experience particularly difficult trading environments. Performance also varies considerably across the textile value chain. Fibre producers are the only segment reporting positive conditions, at +17 percentage points, while spinning mills (-33 percentage points) and textile finishers (-42 percentage points) remain under significant pressure. Textile machinery manufacturers (-35 percentage points) continue to suffer from subdued investment as companies postpone capital expenditure. Despite these challenges, expectations for the next six months have improved to +19 percentage points. However, 46% of respondents anticipate no change in business conditions, suggesting that optimism is not yet supported by clear signs of recovery. content: Kornit Digital Ltd., a global pioneer in on-demand digital fashion and textile production, will showcase the possibilities of digital, on-demand production at PERFORMANCE DAYS 2026, October 13–14 at Messe München, Hall 6, Booth E08. Under the theme “Growth at the speed of demand,” Kornit Digital will demonstrate how digital production can combine design freedom, durability and production flexibility across textile, leather and footwear applications. Together with colortex, Kornit will present a range of real-world applications, including printed leather and footwear, giving visitors the opportunity to see the quality and creative possibilities of digital production firsthand. The applications on display will demonstrate high-definition digital printing across detailed designs, gradients and vibrant colors, alongside custom pattern mapping for individual shoe silhouettes. Visitors will also be able to explore Kornit DuraTech and its possibilities for durable digital applications. “PERFORMANCE DAYS is an opportunity to show what digital production can make possible for performance applications,” said Guy Yaniv, President Kornit Digital Europe. “We’re looking forward to meeting with brands, designers and producers in Munich and demonstrating how on-demand production can bring together creativity, durability and flexibility.” Kornit’s presence at the show will also highlight its broader vision for digital, on-demand production: removing overproduction and manufacturing digitally, in real time. summary: The growing sophistication of engineered textile structures for athletic footwear is being taken a step further with the first industrial installation of Karl Mayer’s new RDJ 7/3 jacquard double needle bar raschel machine. Now operating at Long John Group’s plant in Indonesia, the machine employs three wireless jacquard bars to enable different structures, functional zones […] The post Long John installs Karl Mayer RDJ 7/3 appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: The growing sophistication of engineered textile structures for athletic footwear is being taken a step further with the first industrial installation of Karl Mayer’s new RDJ 7/3 jacquard double needle bar raschel machine. Now operating at Long John Group’s plant in Indonesia, the machine employs three wireless jacquard bars to enable different structures, functional zones and design effects to be positioned within individual footwear fabrics. This allows manufacturers to move beyond uniform textile constructions and engineer different properties into specific areas of a shoe upper, while also introducing complex patterns and three-dimensional effects during fabric production. Among the possibilities are larger and more precisely formed openings, integrated functional and design zones, two-colour jacquard effects and three-dimensional embossed surfaces. The first machine was officially inaugurated at Long John’s Indonesian plant in August in the presence of representatives from international athletic footwear brands and Karl Mayer. Long John celebrates the commissioning of the new RDJ 7/3. © Karl Mayer Taiwan-headquartered Long John is a major supplier of textiles to the global athletic footwear industry, with manufacturing operations in Taiwan, China, Vietnam and Indonesia and a sales office in the USA. Its vertically integrated production encompasses spinning, weaving, knitting, warp knitting, dyeing and finishing, with warp knitting used for open-structure stretch fabrics for shoe uppers and linings as well as spacer fabrics with plain and jacquard-patterned mesh surfaces. Their latest technologies focus on automation, recycling, lower resource use, and better production control. Courtesy: Collected The exhibition will run from Nov. 20 to 24 at the National Exhibition and Convention Center in Shanghai. More than 1,800 companies have applied to exhibit, with nearly 90% of applicants originating from China. The show will also place a stronger emphasis on recycling, automation, digital platforms, and traceability. This makes Shanghai an essential proving ground for the next wave of textile machinery investment across Asia. Members of the Textile Machinery Association of Sweden (TMAS) have introduced several groundbreaking technologies throughout 2026. ACG Kinna has expanded its facility in Skene by 1,000 square meters to support soaring global demand for automated textile and finished-product production systems. Imogo has opened a new showroom, test center, and production facility. Its Dye-Max spray dyeing system processes about 3 tons of fabric per day while using as little as 0.7 liters of dye liquor per kilogram of fabric. This directly targets one of the industry's biggest resource challenges by drastically reducing water, energy, chemical consumption, and wastewater generation. ReSpin implements a different circular approach through its RespinJenny technology. The system mechanically converts textile waste into high-grade fibers for new yarn production and is currently being installed at Sweden’s first industrial spinning mill dedicated entirely to recycled textile fibers. In a conversation with Textile Focus, Dr. Abdul Ahad Akil chief executive officer and director of Karotoa Green Spinning. Figure: Dr. Akil Ahad, CEO & Director at Karotoa Green Spinning Mills Ltd. Dr. Akil Ahad, a resilient and innovative professional, began his journey in 2007 as a trainee at Tara Spinning Mills Ltd. His dedication to the textile industry led him to assume roles such as Director at Karotoa Spinning Mills Ltd. and Deputy Managing Director at Enayetpur Spinning Mills Ltd. In 2018, he ventured into fashion, establishing the successful brand “Lend.” His recent accomplishments include founding Prekite Technologies, an IT and electronics company. and being appointed CEO & Director at Karotoa Green Spinning Mills Ltd. Read the key conversation- Textile Focus: Could you please share with us the current situation of Bangladesh Spinning Sector? Dr. Akil Ahad : Bangladesh’s spinning industry is currently in a strong and positive position, supported by the country’s globally recognized textile and garment sector. Many mills are investing in green manufacturing, automation, recycled yarn, and sustainable production practices to enhance efficiency and meet international standards. The industry’s focus on innovation, sustainability, and quality has increased the confidence of global buyers and strengthened Bangladesh’s reputation as a reliable sourcing destination. With continuous investments and growing demand for sustainable products, the future of Bangladesh’s spinning industry remains highly promising. content: Bangladesh’s garment manufacturers’ association has urged the World Bank to expand funding and the scope of a water security programme to help the country’s apparel industry adopt sustainable water management technologies. The call came at a high-level meeting on Wednesday between Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) President Mahmud Hasan Khan and a World Bank delegation led by Mara K. Warwick, Regional Director for Sustainable Development in South Asia, at the BGMEA complex in Uttara, Dhaka. BGMEA Director Dr. Md. Hasib Uddin also attended the meeting. The World Bank delegation included Lead Water Specialist David Melcom Lord, Senior Water Supply and Sanitation Specialist Rokeya Ahmed, Water Specialist Md. Mahadi Hasan and Environmental Specialist Bushra Nishat. Khan said water management was no longer only an environmental issue but was directly linked to Bangladesh’s international trade and global competitiveness. International buyers, particularly European brands, are increasingly looking for data on water consumption reduction, wastewater treatment and water recycling at different stages of garment production, he said. “There is no alternative to adopting modern water-efficient technologies, both to protect Dhaka’s rivers and groundwater levels and to maintain access to export markets,” Khan said, according to the statement. The meeting reviewed the World Bank-supported Dhaka Water Security and Resilience Program (D-Water) and a $5 million Viability Gap Funding ( VGF ) pilot project under the programme. BGMEA had initially proposed a list of 31 factories for the project, from which the World Bank will begin work with eight factories. title: High fruit yields with 3D fabric
title_ko: 3D 패브릭으로 높은 과일 수확량
summary: A new knitted textile developed at North Carolina State University and used to cover strawberry plants has more than tripled strawberry yields in tunnel field tests – without negatively impacting plant health. The technology could also significantly reduce water and pesticide usage in strawberry fields. The cover, known as Plant Armor, is a carefully designed […] The post High fruit yields with 3D fabric appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: A new knitted textile developed at North Carolina State University and used to cover strawberry plants has more than tripled strawberry yields in tunnel field tests – without negatively impacting plant health. The technology could also significantly reduce water and pesticide usage in strawberry fields. The cover, known as Plant Armor, is a carefully designed fabric that is draped over strawberry plants. The material’s three-dimensional structure prevents insects from reaching the plants beneath, but its multiple layers allow sunlight, rain and airflow to reach the plant. Tunnel field tests found that Plant Armor increased strawberry yields by as much as 3.56 times, without negatively impacting relative humidity or light access. “To produce fruit, plants need sunlight,” said Gabriel Olawuyi, a graduate research assistant at NC State and lead author of a paper on Plant Armor. “We expected that Plant Armor’s seemingly opaque fabric would lead to an increase in vegetative biomass at the expense of fruiting, because reduced sunlight would trigger a ‘shade-avoidance’ response, making the plant divert energy toward stem and leaf growth rather than fruit production. However, we found the fabric did not impede access to light at all, and fruit production increased significantly.” Growing degree days Plant Armor also provided a consistent warming effect over the three seasons that the plant grows, which Olawuyi said helped the bushes reach the fruiting stage earlier than those without the cover. “Plants require a certain amount of accumulated heat, calculated as ‘growing degree-days’, to progress through developmental stages including fruiting. title: BCI reports progress in sustainable cotton
summary: The Better Cotton Initiative (BCI) has published its first Global Impact Report in five years, revealing measurable improvements in the environmental performance and profitability of cotton farming, while highlighting the challenges that remain in achieving consistent progress across different production regions. Released on World Cotton Day on 7 October, the 2026 Global Impact Report draws […] The post BCI reports progress in sustainable cotton appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: The Better Cotton Initiative (BCI) has published its first Global Impact Report in five years, revealing measurable improvements in the environmental performance and profitability of cotton farming, while highlighting the challenges that remain in achieving consistent progress across different production regions. Released on World Cotton Day on 7 October, the 2026 Global Impact Report draws on nine years of field-level data from the world’s largest cotton sustainability programme, which now represents almost a quarter of global cotton production. The findings demonstrate improvements in synthetic fertiliser and pesticide use, greenhouse gas emissions, irrigation water consumption and farmer incomes following adoption of the BCI Standard. This report is an unprecedented and transformative exercise by BCI, as it creates a first step for future programme delivery and deepened impact, with evidence that supports better informed data-driven decisions and scalable actions According to the report, 69% of participating farmers reduced synthetic nitrogen use per kilogram of cotton, while 65% reduced their use of synthetic pesticide active ingredients per hectare. More than half, 54%, lowered their carbon footprint, while 52% of fully irrigated farms reduced the amount of irrigation water applied per kilogram of cotton. The report also identifies improvements in farmer livelihoods, with 59% of smallholder farmers increasing their net income from cotton production since joining the programme. BCI says the findings provide important evidence of how more sustainable agricultural practices can deliver environmental and economic benefits at scale, although the results also underline the complexity of achieving consistent improvements across diverse farming systems. title: From Volume to Value: What BUTEX's new institute must teach to build Bangladesh's advanced textile industry
title_ko: 양에서 가치까지: BUTEX의 새로운 연구소가 Bangladesh의 첨단 섬유 산업을 구축하기 위해 가르쳐야 할 것
summary: The newly approved Institute of Textile Professional Development can do what a garment-export economy has never managed to do: produce the engineers who start medical, geo, aerospace, and electronic t...
content: The newly approved Institute of Textile Professional Development can do what a garment-export economy has never managed to do: produce the engineers who start medical, geo, aerospace, and electronic textile businesses. For four decades, Bangladesh has competed on volume. Readymade garments earned USD 39.35 billion in FY2024-25, according to Export Promotion Bureau data, about four-fifths of the country's USD 48.28 billion merchandise exports. Few countries have built so much export capacity so fast. But in the faster-growing, higher-margin market for technical textiles, Bangladesh is almost invisible. A GIZ feasibility study released with BGMEA in 2021 put the country's share of a global technical textile market worth about USD 180 billion at under half a percent. That is the same country that accounts for more than 6 percent of the world's apparel trade. The recent approval of the Institute of Textile Professional Development (ITPD) at the Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX) is a chance to close that gap. How it is used matters. If ITPD becomes another provider of short courses in merchandising and compliance, it will reinforce the model we already have. If it is designed as a launch pad for advanced textiles, it could become the place where Bangladesh's next export industries are first imagined, tested, and staffed. The constraint is people, not machines The case for ITPD starts with a diagnosis. The GIZ study named five barriers holding back Bangladeshi technical textiles: lack of awareness of market requirements, inadequate technical expertise, difficulty in sourcing high-performance raw materials, compliance and certification requirements, and the need for capital investment. content: India’s domestic apparel market is entering a new phase of sustained growth, with the market projected to rise from US$ 95.7 billion (approximately INR 8 lakh crore) in CY2025 to US$ 146.3 billion (about INR 12 lakh crore) by CY2029, representing a 9% CAGR, according to the Indian Apparel Market Size: A Consumer Research Report 2025, released by the Clothing Manufacturers Association of India (CMAI) in association with 1Lattice, a leading market research consulting organization. Rising casualisation, evolving lifestyles, stronger demand from women and children, increasing preference for comfort and functionality, and the continued importance of physical stores are reshaping how Indians discover, purchase and consume apparel. title: MAAP Adopts Bamboo Rose TotalPLM™ to Accelerate Global Growth
summary: With TotalPLM, MAAP is replacing disconnected workflows with a unified platform. The post MAAP Adopts Bamboo Rose TotalPLM™ to Accelerate Global Growth appeared first on The Interline .
content: BOSTON – October 7, 2026 – Bamboo Rose , a leading end-to-end solution provider for product development and supply chain management, today announced that premium global cycling apparel brand MAAP is adopting Bamboo Rose TotalPLM end-to-end to support its next phase of global growth. By bringing planning, design, product development, sourcing, and order management together on a single AI-native platform, MAAP will give its teams a single connected source of truth from concept to production. As MAAP expanded globally, key workflows remained spread across multiple systems. summary: The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) has called on the World Bank to scale up financial support and expand the scope of funding for sustainable water management in th...
content: The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) has called on the World Bank to scale up financial support and expand the scope of funding for sustainable water management in the country's ready-made garment (RMG) sector. Figure: BGMEA seeks larger World Bank funds for sustainable water management in the RMG sector . Courtesy: Collected The call was made during a high-level bilateral meeting held at the BGMEA Complex in Uttara, Dhaka, on October 7, 2026. Mahmud Hasan Khan, President, BGMEA, led the discussions from the industry side, alongside Dr. Md. Hasib Uddin, Director, BGMEA. Mara K. Warwick, Regional Director for Sustainable Development for the South Asia Region, World Bank, led the visiting high-level delegation. Other key members of the World Bank delegation included David Malcolm Lord, Lead Water Specialist; Rokeya Ahmed, Senior Water Supply and Sanitation Specialist; Md. Mahadi Hasan, Water Specialist; and Bushra Nishat, Environmental Specialist. During the meeting, Mahmud Hasan Khan stated that water management is directly linked to international trade and global competitiveness. He noted that international buyers, especially European brands, prioritize reduced water use, wastewater treatment, and water recycling data. Protecting local water resources is essential to retaining export markets. The meeting reviewed the ongoing Dhaka Water Security and Resilience Program and its 5 million dollar Viability Gap Funding pilot project. BGMEA had proposed 31 factories for the pilot, out of which the World Bank selected eight. Leaders noted that this fund is highly insufficient compared to the massive demand for green technology adoption. content: Author: Stanislas Teisseire, VP of Operations for Inspections & Audits at QIMA For years, the main supply chain story has been China +1, or China + many. Even before tariffs made relying heavily on China too expensive, experienced buyers knew that sourcing from only one country is risky. Most companies now build diversification into their plans, and many are acting on it. Our 2026 Sourcing Survey found 43% of businesses with international sourcing networks changed the countries they sourced from last year. Among US businesses, it was two in three. A lot of investment went into building alternatives. Not many people asked what happens when those alternatives come under pressure too. In our Q3 Barometer , published in July, we saw the first sign of that. Two months later, here’s what has changed and what hasn’t. What we’re seeing In Q2, China represented 35% of our inspections and audits for North American buyers, the highest level in six quarters, while Southeast Asia fell back to pre-2025 levels. The same pattern was visible among EU buyers, but more pronounced. Demand for Southeast Asian inspections weakened every month of the quarter, from 14% growth in April to a 5% decline by June. July, August and early September data suggests this was not a one-time blip. For North American buyers, China’s share kept rising while Southeast Asia’s continued to fall. Likely trigger for the Q2 shift: capacity When the Hormuz crisis cut fuel supply, factories across Southeast and South Asia struggled to keep up. Buyers with peak-season orders had two options. They could accept the delay and risk missing delivery dates, or move some orders to a supplier who could take them. content: Good Earth Cotton (GEC) is advocating a move from broad environmental claims towards measurable evidence as new European Union rules raise the requirements for substantiating sustainability claims. From 27 September, measures implementing the EU’s Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive (EmpCo) began to apply across EU Member States. The rules restrict generic environmental claims that cannot demonstrate recognised environmental performance and prohibit sustainability labels that are not based on approved certification schemes or established by public authorities. The regulatory changes come amid concerns about the credibility of environmental marketing. European Commission analysis has found that 53% of green claims examined in the EU market provide vague, misleading or unfounded information, while 40% have no supporting evidence and half of green labels offer weak or non-existent verification. For Good Earth Cotton, the shift reflects an approach it has been developing over eight years, moving away from practice-based assumptions towards measured outcomes, primary farm-level data, independent verification and fibre physically verified at source. The Australian cotton producer is also deliberately moving beyond the terminology of regenerative agriculture, arguing that describing farming practices does not necessarily demonstrate their environmental outcomes. “For years, we used the language of regenerative agriculture because it helped describe the direction farming needed to take. But a practice is an intervention; an outcome is the evidence,” said Danielle Statham, founder and owner of Good Earth Cotton and FibreTrace. “The next generation of fibre will not be defined by the practice it claims. content: TOKYO — October 1, 2026 — Teijin Frontier Co., Ltd., and Asahi Kasei Advance Co., Ltd., completed the integration of their business operations effective today, and have launched the new entity as TA Frontier Co., Ltd. This integration combines the customer bases and business platforms that the two companies have developed, with the goals of building greater competitiveness, responding more effectively to rapidly changing market conditions and achieving sustainable growth. TA Frontier, the new integrated company, embraces a corporate philosophy of “Creating new value that contribute to a healthy environment and a prosperous future.” It will provide solutions from textiles and apparel to industrial materials, construction materials and resin products that help address challenges in daily life and business across a wide range of industries. “Through this business integration, we have taken a new step forward as TA Frontier Co., Ltd,” stated Susumu Kamata, President and Chief Executive Officer of TA Frontier. “By bringing together the experience, technologies and expertise cultivated by both companies, we will deliver products and services with even greater added value to address the diverse challenges faced by our customers. summary: Jamuna Group has signed a Power Purchase Agreement with GGI for 34 MWp of rooftop solar under an OPEX model, the largest agreement of its kind in Bangladesh to date. Founded in 1974 by Mr. Md. Nurul Islam, Jamuna Group began with Jamuna Electric Manufacturing Co. Ltd. and has since grown into one of Bangladesh’s […] The post Jamuna Group signs PPA with GGI for 34 MWp Rooftop Solar System appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Jamuna Group has signed a Power Purchase Agreement with GGI for 34 MWp of rooftop solar under an OPEX model, the largest agreement of its kind in Bangladesh to date. Founded in 1974 by Mr. Md. Nurul Islam, Jamuna Group began with Jamuna Electric Manufacturing Co. Ltd. and has since grown into one of Bangladesh’s leading conglomerates, with 42 Strategic Business Units spinning textiles, engineering, chemicals, leather, real estate, media, consumer goods and electronics. GGI was jointly established by Heartland, BESTSELLER’s holding company, and SOLshare, and is supported by the ORE Fund from Truvalu and One to Watch. The agreement was signed by Sumaiya Rozalin Islam, Group Director of Jamuna Group and Nure Alam, CEO of Greener Garments Initiative ( GGI ). Under the agreement, GGI will finance, build, own and operate the installations. Jamuna Group will make no upfront investment and will pay a fixed tariff for the electricity generated. Once operational, the system is expected to produce approximately 46,000 MWh of clean electricity and avoid around 30,000 tonnes of CO2 each year, equivalent to the annual absorption of more than one million trees. GGI, jointly established by Heartland ( BESTSELLER.COM ‘s holding company) and ME SOLshare Ltd. , and supported by the ORE Fund from Truvalu Bangladesh and One to Watch , has signed a PPA with Jamuna Group for 34 MWp of rooftop solar under an OPEX model, the largest in Bangladesh so far. As a supplier to BESTSELLER, Jamuna Group’s transition to rooftop solar also contributes to BESTSELLER’s Scope 3 emission reduction targets.With the reduced utility cost of business infrastructures, rooftop solar system is the wheel to move towards the nation’s vision of sustainability. title: Building the Future of Apparel: MAS Expands Its Global and Indian Ambitions
summary: By K. Gopalakrishnan The global apparel industry is undergoing a fundamental transformation. Shorter product cycles, increasingly demanding consumers, the growing importance of performance and functionality, tighter sustainability expectations and rapidly… The post Building the Future of Apparel: MAS Expands Its Global and Indian Ambitions appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: By K. Gopalakrishnan The global apparel industry is undergoing a fundamental transformation. Shorter product cycles, increasingly demanding consumers, the growing importance of performance and functionality, tighter sustainability expectations and rapidly changing sourcing patterns are compelling manufacturers to move beyond the traditional role of production partners. In this evolving landscape, MAS Holdings is positioning itself as a global apparel technology and concept-to-delivery partner, combining product innovation, advanced manufacturing, materials expertise, digital capabilities and responsible production across its international network. Ms. Kam Raghavan, Director – Business Strategy, MAS India With a business of roughly USD 2 billion spanning 13 countries, MAS has progressively evolved from an apparel manufacturer into an integrated partner for leading global brands, with capabilities extending from product development and material selection to manufacturing, supply-chain solutions and innovation. Its expertise in technically demanding categories, supported by a vertically connected ecosystem of fabrics, components, product engineering and digital product development, is enabling the Group to address a much broader part of the customer value chain. India is emerging as an increasingly important component of this global strategy. After around 25 years of operations in the country, MAS is entering a new phase of expansion, driven by the twin opportunities presented by India’s growing domestic apparel market and its potential as a global sourcing and manufacturing hub. content: STOCKHOLM, Sweden — October 7, 2026 — Syre, the textile impact company on a mission to scale textile-to-textile recycling, today announces the appointment of Tim King as its new Chief Executive Officer. Tim King, currently Syre’s Chief Operating Officer, will with his deep experience of Syre’s industrial development, operational leadership, and strategic priorities, lead the company through its next phase of advancement. Tim King Founded in 2023, Syre has established a strong business platform with the industry’s largest commercial agreements, leading industrial partnerships, and a committed investor base. Next step is all about building on that momentum. “We have built a strong foundation, and our focus is to continue turning that into an industrial reality” says Tim King, new CEO of Syre. “I am excited to take on this responsibility and privileged to be working with an exceptional team, supportive customers, and leading partners. Syre’s mission is important for the planet, and we are committed to navigating a challenging market to make circularity a reality at scale”. Tim King has been leading Syre’s industrial development and the execution of strategy since joining Syre in its early days. The conference brought together 71 participants, including 53 factory representatives and 10 members of BKMEA leadership, alongside brands, banks and renewable-energy service providers. Opening the conference, Minhazul Hoque, […] The post BKMEA leadership calls for faster energy transition to secure the future of Bangladesh RMG appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: On 7 October 2026, Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) and ETI Bangladesh jointly organized the second Rapid Energy Transition Conference at BKMEA Bhaban in Narayanganj. The conference brought together 71 participants, including 53 factory representatives and 10 members of BKMEA leadership, alongside brands, banks and renewable-energy service providers. Opening the conference, Minhazul Hoque, Director of BKMEA and Director of Fatullah Dyeing & Calendaring Mills Ltd., urged manufacturers to think beyond immediate compliance and consider where their businesses need to be over the next five to ten years. BKMEA President Mohammad Hatem emphasised that Bangladesh’s garment and textile industry must accelerate renewable-energy adoption and decarbonisation to remain competitive, protect export markets and strengthen long-term business resilience. He urged manufacturers to integrate carbon reduction into factory planning and make use of emerging policy, financing and rooftop-solar opportunities. He also emphasised stronger preparation for LDC graduation, EU requirements and better coordination with government agencies on permissions and approvals. Abil Bin Amin, Executive Director of ETI Bangladesh, said the current energy pressures also create an opportunity for Bangladesh RMG to strengthen its future positioning. He further said “Gradually reducing fossil-fuel dependence and increasing renewable energy can become a business strength and a selling point for Bangladesh’s RMG industry,” Likewise, Eng. Imran Kader Turjo, Director of BKMEA and Managing Director of Southern Knitwear Ltd., warned that failing to prepare for changing market expectations could jeopardise export relationships built over many years. title: Yarn Expo Spring eyes further growth
title_ko: Yarn Expo Spring, 추가 성장 기대
summary: Yarn Expo Spring will return to the National Exhibition and Convention Center in Shanghai from 10–12 March 2027, bringing together international yarn and fibre suppliers, manufacturers and buyers to explore new materials, technologies and sourcing opportunities. The upcoming exhibition follows a record-breaking edition in March 2026, when more than 600 exhibitors from 12 countries and […] The post Yarn Expo Spring eyes further growth appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Yarn Expo Spring will return to the National Exhibition and Convention Center in Shanghai from 10–12 March 2027, bringing together international yarn and fibre suppliers, manufacturers and buyers to explore new materials, technologies and sourcing opportunities. The upcoming exhibition follows a record-breaking edition in March 2026, when more than 600 exhibitors from 12 countries and regions connected with over 25,000 visitors from 113 countries and regions. The strong participation reinforced the event’s position as an important international platform for yarn and fibre sourcing, innovation and industry exchange. Organised by Messe Frankfurt (HK) Ltd and the Sub-Council of Textile Industry, CCPIT, the exhibition will once again take place alongside Intertextile Shanghai Apparel Fabrics – Spring Edition, Intertextile Shanghai Home Textiles – Spring Edition, CHIC and PH Value, creating opportunities for businesses across the textile and apparel supply chain. The fair provided an exceptional platform for connecting with the global textile community Wilmet Shea, General Manager of Messe Frankfurt (HK) Ltd, said: “In a changing economic landscape, last year’s record participation showed how important it is for the yarn and fibre industry to meet in Shanghai, exchange ideas and understand what the market needs next.” She added that suppliers would have opportunities to present their latest developments to buyers from apparel, home textiles, knitting and related sectors, while discussing requirements and establishing long-term business relationships. The exhibition comes as the global yarn, fibre and thread market continues to evolve, with research forecasting its value to reach US$182.7 billion by 2032. title: Technical textiles market set to reach $318.7 billion by 2031
title_ko: 산업용 섬유 시장은 2031년까지 3,187억 달러에 이를 것으로 예상됩니다.
summary: The global technical textiles market is entering a steady expansion phase as industries demand advanced, high-performance materials. Market research from BCC Research shows the sector was valued at $2...
content: The global technical textiles market is entering a steady expansion phase as industries demand advanced, high-performance materials. Market research from BCC Research shows the sector was valued at $228.7 billion in 2025 and is projected to hit $318.7 billion by 2031, growing at a compound annual growth rate of 5.9% from 2026 to 2031. Figure: Technical textiles market set to reach $318.7 billion by 2031. Courtesy: Collected This growth reflects a major shift toward engineering fabrics for specific industrial needs rather than conventional apparel, leveraging strength, low weight, and durability. Asia-Pacific anchors this expansion, currently holding 38.1% of the global market with its massive manufacturing base and competitive costs. Government initiatives like India's Production Linked Incentive scheme are accelerating this momentum by approving around $1.2 to $1.3 billion to build domestic capacity. Healthcare is also fueling demand through rising medical spending and an increase in specialized surgical procedures. Medtech innovations now span advanced wound care, biocompatible implants, and wearable health-monitoring devices that require antimicrobial performance. At the same time, cutting-edge technologies are expanding capabilities, with nanotechnology projected to grow at a 7.3% compound annual growth rate and 3D weaving expected to grow at 6.7% through 2031. Ultimately, these advancements are paving the way for self-decontaminating fabrics through metal-organic framework materials and smart e-textiles. The market outlook proves that technical textiles are becoming deeply intertwined with broader industrial innovation, where long-term success relies heavily on developing specialized materials.

summary: “3D in BD — Discovered, Designed & Developed in Bangladesh” Design in Bangladesh Week 2026 officially opened at the United Convention Centre, Dhaka, bringing 100 Bangladeshi designers onto one collective platform and runway to showcase the country’s growing capacity in design, creativity, craftsmanship, innovation, product development and creative entrepreneurship. The inaugural ceremony was graced by […] The post Design In Bangladesh Week – Bangladesh’s Next Design Generation Takes Centre Stage With 100 Designers Runway appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: “3D in BD — Discovered, Designed & Developed in Bangladesh” Design in Bangladesh Week 2026 officially opened at the United Convention Centre, Dhaka, bringing 100 Bangladeshi designers onto one collective platform and runway to showcase the country’s growing capacity in design, creativity, craftsmanship, innovation, product development and creative entrepreneurship. The inaugural ceremony was graced by Dr. S. M. Ziauddin Hyder, Special Assistant to the Honorable Prime Minister on Health Affairs, with the status of State Minister, as Chief Guest. In his address, Dr. Hyder welcomed the participation and work of 100 designers and encouraged the Design in Bangladesh platform to continue developing as a collaborative creative hub connecting talent, heritage, enterprise, industry and opportunity. He also highlighted the relevance of “One Village, One Product” and the 3D in BD vision — Discovered, Designed & Developed in Bangladesh — as approaches that can help create greater value from Bangladesh’s own creative capacity. Design in Bangladesh Week positions design as an important contributor to Bangladesh’s creative economy — connecting original ideas and cultural knowledge with research, product development, manufacturing, branding, entrepreneurship and market access. The initiative seeks to complement the country’s wider ambition to strengthen innovation, value addition and creative enterprise by building stronger connections between creative talent and Bangladesh’s established production ecosystem. 100 DESIGNERS — ONE PLATFORM At the heart of the opening was the 100 Designers Showcase and Runway, bringing together 100 creative voices on one shared platform. title_ko: AeoniQ, 첫 번째 상용 물량 마감
summary: Swiss cellulosic filament developer AeoniQ expects to begin supplying initial market volumes in early 2027 as it makes the transition from pilot development towards industrial production in Portugal. Returning to the Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress in Austria from September 16-18, five years after its technology was first presented at the event’s Innovation Days, AeoniQ outlined […] The post AeoniQ closes in on first commercial volumes appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Swiss cellulosic filament developer AeoniQ expects to begin supplying initial market volumes in early 2027 as it makes the transition from pilot development towards industrial production in Portugal. Returning to the Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress in Austria from September 16-18, five years after its technology was first presented at the event’s Innovation Days, AeoniQ outlined the progress made towards commercialising a biodegradable filament designed as an alternative to polyester and nylon. The technology converts cellulose into continuous filament yarn which can subsequently be texturised, dyed, woven or knitted using conventional textile machinery. Its feedstock flexibility is also central to the longer-term proposition. In addition to wood-derived cellulose, AeoniQ is exploring recycled textile cellulose, agricultural residues and bacterial cellulose as potential raw material sources. The major change since its first Dornbirn appearance has been the involvement of Portuguese pulp and forest products group Altri, which acquired a 58.7% interest in AeoniQ Holding in 2025. A pre-industrial production unit is now being established in Portugal to support product development and initial market programmes, while a larger industrial plant is planned at Altri’s Caima pulp operation in Constância. The first industrial unit is planned with annual capacity of around 1,750 tons. Altri has indicated that construction is scheduled to start in 2027, with the full project targeted to start production in 2028. AeoniQ global director of business development Carmen Danner said that initial market volumes from the pre-industrial operation are expected from January 2027. content: Bangladesh is seeking to expand its readymade garment exports to Indonesia as the two countries revisit stalled trade negotiations, highlighting a largely untapped apparel market despite their position as competitors in the global textile and clothing industry. Figure: Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, Commerce Minister, made a courtesy call on a meeting with Mohammad Anis Matta, Deputy Foreign Minister, Indonesia, at the Commerce Ministry on 7th Oct. Courtesy:Collected The push gained fresh momentum on October 7 during a high-level meeting at the Commerce Ministry, where Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, Minister, Ministry of Commerce, discussed bilateral trade with visiting Mohammad Anis Matta, Deputy Foreign Minister, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Indonesia. The trade minister noted that bilateral commerce could rise significantly if market-access barriers are removed. Bangladesh currently exports about $56 million worth of goods to Indonesia while importing around $3.5 billion, leaving a substantial trade deficit. For Bangladesh's apparel sector, Indonesia remains a relatively small destination. Yet according to UN Comtrade data, the latest product-level figures show a meaningful existing market. Indonesia imported $48.41 million worth of apparel from Bangladesh in 2025, comprising $26.26 million in non-knit garments and $22.15 million in knitwear. According to UN Comtrade data, the product mix points to opportunities across several categories. Indonesia imported $8.44 million of Bangladeshi T-shirts, $4.63 million of sweaters, pullovers and vests, and $2.07 million of men's knitted shirts in 2025. title: Is AI Already Good Enough For Fashion?
summary: When it comes to visually representing a product, and building alignment around that visualisation, brands and retailers are placing some serious bets on the capabilities of both general-purpose frontier models and fashion-specific tooling. But is AI “good enough” to change the overall go-to-market trajectory? The post Is AI Already Good Enough For Fashion? appeared first on The Interline .
content: Hey, welcome back to The Interline Podcast. Is AI ‘good enough’? That might just be the central question at the current moment. If you go looking, you can find evidence to support both answers. I’ll put our evidence first, because it’s the data I have closest to hand. We surveyed about 100 fashion professionals earlier this year. They are broadly optimistic about AI, but in the here and now they report that they don’t trust it with critical decisions. They don’t have a good rubric for assessing its value. They fear that their companies are overestimating its capabilities versus what it can actually deliver. They consequently haven’t connected it to their wider tech estates. Good enough? Maybe. But the size of the market and the investment statistics that brands themselves are disclosing to us suggest that the available applications clearly are good enough to invest in. Nine in ten professionals use AI every day at work in some capacity. Nearly 85% of companies have accelerated their adoption of AI in the last twelve months. Almost 70% expect their spending on it to increase as we go into 2027. You can also look at the huge landscape of AI tools for fashion that exist, both as additional capabilities bolted onto existing solutions, as pivots, and as whole new platforms built with AI as their foundations. There’s a lot of all of those. We interviewed some of the executives behind all those types of tools in the same AI Report that the survey data I just mentioned is taken from. I think it’s fair to say that they all see a pretty unprecedented market opportunity in front of them. summary: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has signed two loan agreements totaling $275 million and a $2.72 million grant with the Government of Bangladesh to implement vital infrastructure and community empowe...
content: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has signed two loan agreements totaling $275 million and a $2.72 million grant with the Government of Bangladesh to implement vital infrastructure and community empowerment projects. Figure: Md. Shahriar Kader Siddiky, Secretary, Economic Relations Division, and Qingfeng Zhang, Country Director, Asian Development Bank, exchange documents after signing loan and grant agreements between the Government of Bangladesh and the Asian Development Bank in Dhaka on 7 th Oct. Courtesy: Collected The financing agreements were signed on 7 th Oct by Md. Shahriar Kader Siddiky, Secretary, Economic Relations Division (ERD) and Qingfeng Zhang, Country Director, ADB Bangladesh Resident Mission. The initiative includes a $100 million loan for the Inclusive Affordable Housing Finance Project, implemented through the Palli Karma-Sahayak Foundation (PKSF) to expand climate-resilient housing for low- and middle-income families. Additionally, a $175 million loan and a $2.72 million grant funded by the Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific (JFPAR) will support the Sustainable Energy Development and Community Empowerment in the Hill Tracts Project. Both loans carry a 2 percent annual interest rate. They feature a 25-year repayment term, which includes a five-year grace period. These projects directly target regional energy access and housing. At the same time, stable power infrastructure and sustainable regional development serve as critical indirect catalysts for the broader macro-economy and export sectors. Reliable green energy expansion helps mitigate national power grid vulnerabilities. This lowers operational disruptions for manufacturing supply chains. Md. Salauddin, Director, Reaz Garments Ltd., shared his industry experience and discussed the skills young professionals will […] The post Future Skills: Preparing the Next Generation of RMG Professionals appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: A webinar on “Future Skills in RMG & Textile and AI Tools in RMG”, organised by Textile Times, brought together around 100 Textile Engineering students and RMG professionals for a practical discussion on the future of the industry. Md. Salauddin, Director, Reaz Garments Ltd., shared his industry experience and discussed the skills young professionals will need as the RMG sector moves towards technology, sustainability and higher productivity. Shohel Hossen Saikat, Founder of ecoeen, Co-Founder of Bunon Bee and Lead Trainer of AI Mastery 360, discussed the growing role of AI tools in RMG. The key takeaway from the session was that a degree alone will not be enough for tomorrow’s job market. Future professionals will need to continuously develop skills in AI, digital technology, data analysis, sustainability, communication and problem-solving. The speakers also encouraged students to become problem solvers rather than simply job seekers and to view AI as a tool that can enhance their capabilities, not just a threat to employment. The session was part of the ongoing knowledge-sharing mission of Bunon & TGM Blog, connecting industry experience with the next generation of textile and RMG leaders. summary: WEST JORDAN, Utah — September 23, 2026 — Chloris is strengthening the commercial readiness of its flagship bio-based dye, Claessen Blue™, through a growing international verification framework covering bio-based origin, traceability, responsible chemical management and textile application. Rather than treating individual certifications as standalone credentials, Chloris has organized them around the key questions brands, mills […]
content: WEST JORDAN, Utah — September 23, 2026 — Chloris is strengthening the commercial readiness of its flagship bio-based dye, Claessen Blue , through a growing international verification framework covering bio-based origin, traceability, responsible chemical management and textile application. Rather than treating individual certifications as standalone credentials, Chloris has organized them around the key questions brands, mills and manufacturers need to address when evaluating a new material. Bio-based Origin — USDA BioPreferred® and OK biobased provide independent verification of bio-based carbon content, supporting clear and credible renewable-material claims. Traceability — ISCC PLUS extends verification into renewable feedstocks and chain-of-custody traceability, connecting material sourcing with industrial production. Chemical Safety — ZDHC MRSL Level 3 and OEKO-TEX® support chemical management and textile chemical safety requirements relevant to global sourcing and manufacturing. Application Approval — GOTS Approved Input supports the use of Claessen Blue within GOTS-certified textile processing, subject to applicable requirements. In parallel, Chloris uses Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) as a separate layer of quantitative environmental evidence. While certification verifies attributes, processes and compliance pathways, LCA evaluates environmental performance within defined life-cycle boundaries. This provides brands and supply-chain partners with measurable evidence across relevant environmental indicators and helps translate sustainability from a material claim into data that can inform sourcing and ESG decisions. content: BRUSSELS — October 5, 2026 — ReHubs has appointed Béatrice Moureaux as Chief Executive Officer, marking a new chapter for the European alliance as it continues to strengthen its work to scale textile-to-textile recycling across Europe. Béatrice Moureaux Béatrice has served as Board Advisor to ReHubs since December 2025, working closely with its Board, team and members on the organisation’s strategy and projects. She brings more than 25 years of experience across technical textiles, advanced fibres, nonwovens and circular innovation. Her appointment comes at a challenging time for Europe’s textile circularity transition. Despite advances in technology and growing policy ambition, the conditions needed to scale textile-to-textile recycling remain difficult. Recyclers need greater certainty of demand to invest in capacity, while brands need reliable and competitive supplies of recycled fibres to commit to greater volumes. ReHubs’ strategy is focused on breaking this supply-demand deadlock. As a membership-based organisation, ReHubs brings together leading organisations from across the textile value chain to strengthen collaboration, improve the conditions for investment and support the development of a viable textile-to-textile recycling industry in Europe. Commenting on her appointment, Béatrice Moureaux, CEO of ReHubs, shares: “I’m proud to take on the role of CEO at such an important moment for ReHubs and our industry. The road ahead will be challenging, and breaking the supply-demand deadlock to scale textile-to-textile recycling in Europe will require an openness to collaboration across the value chain and the right conditions for investment. content: NEUBULACH, Germany — October 1, 2026 — Faster support, shorter lead times and local technical expertise: customers in Peru, Colombia, and Ecuador now have direct access to Trützschler Card Clothing’s (TCC) comprehensive card clothing services. To further enhance customer support and ensure rapid on-site assistance, TCC has expanded its regional service network across all three countries. From left to right: Yohan Danilo Avendaño, Rodolfo Quichiz (Tejidos Jorgito), Héctor Montenegro (Redimtex), and Abraham Cárdenas (Tejidos Jorgito) at the TRÜTZSCHLER service station at Tejidos Jorgito. The expansion reflects Trützschler’ s commitment to the Andean region for the textile and nonwovens industries. Peru is home to one of South America’s most established spinning sectors, built on its renowned Pima and Tangüis cotton production. In Colombia and Ecuador, spinning and nonwovens manufacturers continue to invest in quality and productivity improvements. By strengthening its local presence in the region, TCC can respond more quickly to customer needs. Professional card clothing service plays a key role in maintaining consistently high carding performance: precise mounting, optimized machine settings and expert troubleshooting help mills maximize clothing lifetime, ensure stable product quality and maintain efficient production. To provide this support directly where it is needed, TCC has established workshop partnerships with long-standing customers in each of the three countries. title: BTU-TECH Introduces BTU-GMAX, Delivering Premium Multiaxial Production Flexibility At An Entry-Level Investment Range
title_ko: BTU-TECH, 보급형 투자 범위에서 프리미엄 다축 생산 유연성을 제공하는 BTU-GMAX 출시
summary: ISTANBUL — September 29, 2026 — BTU-TECH has announced the launch of BTU-GMAX, a next-generation multiaxial production line developed to deliver the flexibility of advanced multiaxial platforms at an investment level comparable to conventional entry-level machines. With its fully programmable 0°–180° weft-angle capability, BTU-GMAX enables manufacturers to produce a wide range of multiaxial fabric architectures, mainly […]
content: ISTANBUL — September 29, 2026 — BTU-TECH has announced the launch of BTU-GMAX, a next-generation multiaxial production line developed to deliver the flexibility of advanced multiaxial platforms at an investment level comparable to conventional entry-level machines. With its fully programmable 0°–180° weft-angle capability, BTU-GMAX enables manufacturers to produce a wide range of multiaxial fabric architectures, mainly glass, aramid, carbon fabrics for composite industries, on a single platform. Operators can select new production angles directly from the interface without lengthy mechanical adjustments. One of the system’s key innovations is its ability to calculate weft paths directly on the industrial motion controller in real time. New production parameters can be applied within seconds without external computer software, CAM table generation, or a machine restart. This significantly reduces setup times and increases machine availability. BTU-GMAX uses a heavy-duty trigger-belt-driven carrier architecture instead of conventional rack-driven systems. The design reduces wear and noise, improves positional accuracy, prevents jump-offs at high speed, and simplifies maintenance. Built on BTU-TECH’s proprietary PC-free automation platform, the system combines real-time weft-curve calculation, automatic carrier synchronization at every production start, and electronic collision prevention. Integrated laser safety barriers dynamically monitor operator positioning, while Industry 4.0 connectivity allows production data and machine parameters to be transferred to ERP systems and factory networks via industrial communication protocols. content: MADRID – Recover has launched a new range of cotton-polyester fibre blends made from recycled materials which it says can eliminate the need for downstream overdyeing. The Spanish textile recycler’s product range, Recover One, combines its mechanically recycled cotton with colour-matched, dope-dyed recycled polyester to create ready-to-spin blends for textile manufacturers. The technology uses an intimate blending process that harmonises the colours of recycled textile feedstocks with recycled polyester fibres. According to Recover, this produces a consistent material without the need for additional overdyeing, potentially reducing processing time, water consumption and production costs. The blends are available in different cotton-polyester ratios, depending on the intended application. They can be supplied either as fibre or finished fabric through Recover’s supply chain partners. Applications include single jersey, French terry and fleece fabrics, with solid, heather and mélange colour options available. “With Recover One, we are making it easier for brands and manufacturers to use recycled materials at scale,” said Enes Adak, co-CEO and chief product officer at Recover. “By combining our recycled cotton with recycled polyester, we deliver a consistent blend that simplifies production and helps reduce costs. This brings sustainability and business value together.” Recover says the product builds on the environmental advantages of its recycled cotton, while delivering additional savings by removing the overdyeing stage. content: PORTUGAL — October 8, 2026 — Selenis, the only specialty copolyester producer manufacturing in Europe, has acquired the production assets of Polisan Hellas in Greece for installation in Portugal. Including these assets, Selenis will operate more than 200,000 metric tonnes (MT) of annual installed specialty copolyester capacity by 2028, across production sites in Portugal, Italy, Tunisia and the United States. The acquisition adds continuous polymerisation to a manufacturing base built on flexibility. Continuous production serves the high-volume markets, where standardisation, consistency and cost per tonne matter. Selenis investment supports growth in four priority markets, Texnascis , Shrink sleeves, Selcare® and Mimesis Batch production serves specialty and custom grades, where smaller volumes, fast changeovers and formulation depth are key. With both technologies now part of its manufacturing platform across four countries, Selenis can serve the full spectrum of the market, from high-volume applications to specialised grades, combining the scale and efficiency of continuous production with the flexibility of batch manufacturing. “We believe Europe needs a strong specialty materials manufacturing base, and we are investing to build it,” said Duarte Matos Gil, CEO of Selenis. “When customers qualify our materials, they make a long-term commitment. Our responsibility is to invest ahead of their needs, to put more than one plant behind every grade and to give them a cost base that lets them compete. summary: Selenis, the only specialty copolyester producer manufacturing in Europe, has acquired the production assets of Polisan Hellas in Greece for installation in Portugal. Including these assets, Selenis will operate more than 200,000 metric tons of annual installed specialty copolyester capacity by 2028, across production sites in Portugal, Italy, Tunisia and the United States. The acquisition […] The post Selenis acquires Polisan Hellas appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Selenis, the only specialty copolyester producer manufacturing in Europe, has acquired the production assets of Polisan Hellas in Greece for installation in Portugal. Including these assets, Selenis will operate more than 200,000 metric tons of annual installed specialty copolyester capacity by 2028, across production sites in Portugal, Italy, Tunisia and the United States. The acquisition adds continuous polymerisation to a manufacturing base built on flexibility. Continuous production serves the high-volume markets, where standardisation, consistency and cost per ton matter, while batch production serves speciality and custom grades, where smaller volumes, fast changeovers and formulation depth are key. With both technologies now part of its manufacturing platform across four countries, Selenis can serve the full spectrum of the market, from high-volume applications to specialised grades, combining the scale and efficiency of continuous production with the flexibility of batch manufacturing. “We believe Europe needs a strong speciality materials manufacturing base and we are investing to build it,” said Duarte Matos Gil, CEO of Selenis. “When customers qualify our materials, they make a long-term commitment. Our responsibility is to invest ahead of their needs, to put more than one plant behind every grade and to give them a cost base that lets them compete. This acquisition puts industrial capacity behind that commitment, and further steps will follow.” Selenis will work with customers to qualify selected grades at more than one manufacturing site, so a converter can hold the same specification from two plants, with no dependency on a single line or region and with the flexibility to move volume between sites as demand and logistics change. So, if you were to ask me: is it today? No. Is it tomorrow? Yes. What’s working is the growing alignment around data, transparency, and outcome-based approaches. title: Beximco seeks approval to reopen factory with $23mn foreign investment
summary: Beximco Group is seeking government approval for a leasing plan to partially reopen a closed garment factory at its Gazipur industrial park. The move involves British and Chinese investors aiming to r...
content: Beximco Group is seeking government approval for a leasing plan to partially reopen a closed garment factory at its Gazipur industrial park. The move involves British and Chinese investors aiming to revive production and boost export capacity. Under the proposed five-year arrangement, British firm Charter HCP Ltd and Chinese company Besting Ltd plan to invest $23 million to restart Prefix Fashions Ltd at Beximco Industrial Park in Kashimpur. Khalid Shahrior, Chief HR & Compliance Officer at Beximco Textiles, Apparel & PPE Division and Huda Mohammed Faisal, CEO of Revival Global, which is acting as an asset manager for the investors, confirmed the plan. Beximco officials are scheduled to meet the chairman of Invest Bangladesh on October 11 to discuss the proposed leasing model. The arrangement would also require approval from Invest Bangladesh and Bangladesh Bank. If approved, the factory is expected to resume operations in April next year, primarily producing export-oriented jackets. Around 90% of its production would focus on jackets, while the remaining 10% would cover other apparel products. The factory is expected to initially employ around 2,500 workers. The investors estimate that the unit could export garments worth about $500 million within two to three years, with Besting’s international retail and brand network expected to support order generation. Prefix Fashions is one of 16 textile and garment units located inside the Beximco Industrial Park. According to Beximco officials, the factory has been a joint venture with Besting since its establishment. A key feature of the proposed model is the repayment mechanism. The foreign investors would sign a five-year agreement with Beximco, while loan repayments would be made directly from the factory’s export proceeds

summary: Dimension-Polyant is extending the sailcloth-derived technology behind its X-Pac technical fabrics with a new family of lightweight laminates aimed at mountaineering, climbing, skiing and bikepacking equipment. The new X-Pac hyperTEC range will make its European debut at Performance Days in Munich from October 13-14, where the company will show its first UX10 and UX20 sT […] The post X-Pac takes sailcloth technology into outdoor fabrics appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Dimension-Polyant is extending the sailcloth-derived technology behind its X-Pac technical fabrics with a new family of lightweight laminates aimed at mountaineering, climbing, skiing and bikepacking equipment. The new X-Pac hyperTEC range will make its European debut at Performance Days in Munich from October 13-14, where the company will show its first UX10 and UX20 sT constructions. The X-Pac fabrics originated from Dimension-Polyant’s experience in high-performance sailcloth, applying similar precision lamination techniques to fabrics. At the centre of the construction is a 100% Ultra-PE face fabric combined with X-Pac’s Ultra-PE X-Ply reinforcement. The laminate construction also provides inherent waterproofing. “Using advanced fibres allows us to produce laminates that are ultra-light and have a tremendous strength-to-weight ratio, while maintaining the durability and reliability that X-Pac is known for,” said Dimension-Polyant president Kenneth Madsen. Two versions will initially be highlighted in Munich. X-Pac hyperTEC UX10, available in translucent white, has been developed as the more versatile of the two, balancing low weight and durability for packs across a range of outdoor applications. UX20 sT, in black, places greater emphasis on strength and load-bearing performance for more highly stressed applications. The “sT” refers to a single polyester taffeta backing layer positioned behind the polyester film, improving handling and durability and giving the otherwise lightweight laminate a more opaque appearance. One of the first commercial adopters is Belgian bikepacking specialist Moga Bags, which is introducing products manufactured with hyperTEC fabrics. title: Fashion for Good launches Cotton Reloop Matrix to scale recycled cotton use
title_ko: Fashion for Good, 재활용 면 사용 확대를 위해 Cotton Reloop Matrix 출시
summary: Fashion for Good has launched the Cotton Reloop Matrix Project to improve the use of mechanically recycled cotton in textile production. The project aims to connect the capabilities of cotton recycle...
content: Fashion for Good has launched the Cotton Reloop Matrix Project to improve the use of mechanically recycled cotton in textile production. The project aims to connect the capabilities of cotton recyclers with the quality requirements of fashion brands. It will also address gaps in testing and data sharing across the supply chain. Major stakeholders, including Arvind, Bestseller, C&A, Interloop, Reformation, Shahi, and Uster, are taking part in the project. The initiative has two main tracks. The first will assess recycled cotton yarn performance for knit and woven fabrics. It will focus on whether the yarn is suitable for its intended use rather than comparing it directly with virgin cotton. The project will also explore performance levels beyond the current typical 10% recycled cotton blend limit. The second track will include trials to produce 10 demonstration fabrics and conduct five process-optimization trials. The findings will be published in an open-source Standard Operating Procedure (SOP). This will help standardize spinning parameters across different supply chains. The project aims to create clearer quality benchmarks and help overcome fiber degradation challenges. It could support wider and more commercial use of recycled cotton in the global textile industry.

title: Empowering and Equipping Cotton Farmers with Regenerative Practices in Maharashtra
title_ko: 마하라슈트라의 목화 재배자들에게 재생 관행을 제공하고 지원
summary: Words by Zoë Goodhead, with photography by Abhishek Khedekar In villages in the Amravati region in Maharashtra, India, farmers are coming together to share knowledge and learn regenerative practices for […] The post Empowering and Equipping Cotton Farmers with Regenerative Practices in Maharashtra appeared first on Textile Exchange .
content: Words by Zoë Goodhead, with photography by Abhishek Khedekar In villages in the Amravati region in Maharashtra, India, farmers are coming together to share knowledge and learn regenerative practices for their small-scale cotton farms. As the scheme grows, they are discovering that these practices can not only save them money, but also save their soil. At Nagpur airport, welcome signs declare it the City of Oranges, but driving through the Maharashtra landscape towards the Amravati region, it’s not just orange trees that can be seen growing in the fields, but cotton, with balls of white catching the light of the sun. The connection with this cotton is deeply felt by those who spend their days sowing, growing, and picking it. Madhuri Anil Dugane, from Kati, a small village in Amravati, describes her special relationship with the soil. “My connection with the soil feels like one between a mother and a daughter,” she explains in Marathi, the local language. “Unless you work hard at it, unless you love your mother, how can you expect to get anything out of it?” Madhuri has always lived in Kati, surrounded by cotton fields. She now lives with her husband and two children, farming cotton on her own land and also picking up shifts as a laborer on other nearby farms for extra income. Along with others in her village, she has recently signed up to CottonConnect’s REEL Regenerative program. CottonConnect works with local partner Apeksha Homoeo Society to roll out the program in villages across the region, working with around 4,500 farmers in just this area alone. This is just one of many projects for Apeksha, a local charitable organization ensuring the sustainable development of women, children, farmers, and landless communities. title: Cotton remains vital to a changing global textile industry
title_ko: 면화는 변화하는 글로벌 섬유 산업에 여전히 중요한 역할을 하고 있습니다.
summary: World Cotton Day 2026 is being observed on October 7, highlighting the continued importance of cotton to global agriculture, textile production, international trade and the livelihoods of millions of...
content: World Cotton Day 2026 is being observed on October 7, highlighting the continued importance of cotton to global agriculture, textile production, international trade and the livelihoods of millions of people. The United Nations officially designated October 7 as World Cotton Day through a resolution adopted by the UN General Assembly on August 30, 2021. The initiative was originally proposed by four major African cotton-producing countries—Benin, Burkina Faso, Chad and Mali, collectively known as the Cotton-4. The day aims to raise global awareness of cotton’s contribution to economic development and highlight the challenges faced by farmers, producers, processors and workers across the cotton value chain. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), International Trade Centre, UN Conference on Trade and Development and International Cotton Advisory Committee supported the initiative before its formal adoption by the UN. Cotton remains one of the world's most important natural fibers and a key raw material for the global textile and apparel industry. Around 80% of cotton is used for clothing, while another 15% is used for home textiles and other household products, according to FAO data. Beyond its role as a textile fiber, cotton is an important source of income for millions of farming households. Around 24 million producers are involved in cotton cultivation globally, while the wider sector supports more than 100 million families through farming, processing, manufacturing and trade. For many developing economies, cotton exports are also an important source of foreign exchange. As a result, changes in global cotton prices, production and demand can have a direct impact on farmers and national economies. Global cotton production remains substantial.

content: GENEVA – Every Brazilian farmer included in Better Cotton Initiative’s hazardous-pesticide reporting used highly hazardous pesticides in 2024–25, according to its latest impact report. The findings expose the scale of the challenge facing BCI’s regenerative ambitions in a country that supplied more than half its cotton in 2023–24. Brazil produced approximately three million tonnes of BCI cotton that season, out of 5.64 million tonnes globally. Its 53 per cent share gives Brazilian farming practices a substantial influence over the scheme’s environmental performance. title: Mohammad Faizul Alam Becomes Vice President of MICE Association Bangladesh
summary: Mohammad Faizul Alam, Managing Director of Savor International Limited, has become the Vice President of MICE Association Bangladesh, an industry platform representing the Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE) sector in Bangladesh. Savor International Limited is a key player in Bangladesh’s MICE industry, particularly in the exhibition sector, with a growing footprint in both domestic […] The post Mohammad Faizul Alam Becomes Vice President of MICE Association Bangladesh appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Mohammad Faizul Alam, Managing Director of Savor International Limited, has become the Vice President of MICE Association Bangladesh, an industry platform representing the Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE) sector in Bangladesh. Savor International Limited is a key player in Bangladesh’s MICE industry, particularly in the exhibition sector, with a growing footprint in both domestic and international markets. Beyond Savor International, Mr. Alam serves as Managing Director of Postmaster Communication and Springfield Corporation, the official channel partner of Alibaba.com in Bangladesh. He is also the Executive Director of British Columbia School. Mr. Alam is actively involved in various chambers and trade associations. He currently serves as a Director of the Bangladesh-Malaysia Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BMCCI) and as Advisor to the President of the Bangladesh China Chamber of Commerce & Industry (BCCCI). Through his involvement in business, international trade, exhibitions and industry associations, he continues to contribute to strengthening Bangladesh’s MICE ecosystem and expanding its international connectivity.
