title: BTMA seeks policy support to protect primary textile industry
summary: A BTMA delegation led by President Shawkat Aziz Russell has urged stronger policy support to protect Bangladesh’s primary textile industry. They emphasized increasing local value addition and safeguar...
content: A BTMA delegation led by President Shawkat Aziz Russell has urged stronger policy support to protect Bangladesh’s primary textile industry. They emphasized increasing local value addition and safeguarding competitiveness after LDC graduation. The delegation met Dr Shafiqul Rahman, MP, Leader of the Opposition in the National Parliament, at his official residence on Minto Road following his invitation. The BTMA delegation outlined the current situation, prospects, and challenges of the primary textile and spinning industry, and elaborated on the policy support required for sustainable development. They noted that the delegation had already met the Prime Minister twice, leading to the formation of a high-level inter-ministerial committee to address sectoral issues. Following the committee’s guidance, BTMA submitted a comprehensive proposal to the relevant ministries, which is now under active government consideration. To safeguard the national economy, employment, foreign exchange savings, and post‑LDC graduation export capacity, BTMA presented proposals seeking policy support in the following areas: Ensuring raw materials for export-oriented industries Preserving the capacity of domestic primary textile industry Increasing local value addition Protecting employment Saving and conserving foreign exchange Securing government revenue Preventing misuse of bond facilities and illegal imports The Opposition Leader listened attentively and emphasized that a balanced and coordinated policy could sustainably strengthen Bangladesh’s primary textile industry, reinforce export capacity, and solidify the industrial base. title: EAS: Turning Textile Data into Actionable Intelligence
title_ko: EAS: 섬유 데이터를 실행 가능한 인텔리전스로 전환
summary: By K. Gopalakrishnan As textile manufacturers move towards connected, data-driven production, EAS is bringing together ERP, MES, industrial automation, machinery connectivity and automated dosing systems to create a more integrated… The post EAS: Turning Textile Data into Actionable Intelligence appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: By K. Gopalakrishnan As textile manufacturers move towards connected, data-driven production, EAS is bringing together ERP, MES, industrial automation, machinery connectivity and automated dosing systems to create a more integrated Industry 4.0 environment. Francesc López, Area Manager – India & Asia, EAS, outlines how the company is helping mills improve visibility, traceability, productivity and resource efficiency, with India emerging as a strategic market for its next phase of growth. For more than three decades, EAS – Escarré Automatización y Servicios has focused on applying automation and digital technologies to solve practical challenges in textile manufacturing. Founded in Barcelona in 1991, the company has evolved from a specialist in industrial automation and process control into a technology partner offering production-management software, MES solutions, data acquisition, industrial connectivity, automated chemical and dye preparation systems and specialised machinery. Its solutions today operate in more than 35 countries. Francesc López, Area Manager – India & Asia, EAS According to Francesc López, Area Manager – India & Asia, EAS, the company’s evolution has been driven by a simple principle: technology must serve the production process. This philosophy is particularly relevant as textile manufacturers seek to connect increasingly complex machinery environments while gaining greater control over productivity, quality, traceability and resource consumption. From Automation Supplier to Digital Ecosystem EAS brings together three areas that are often managed independently: software, industrial automation and machinery. summary: “3D in BD — Discovered, Designed & Developed in Bangladesh” Design in Bangladesh Week 2026 officially opened at the United Convention Centre, Dhaka, bringing 100 Bangladeshi designers onto one collective platform and runway to showcase the country’s growing capacity in design, creativity, craftsmanship, innovation, product development and creative entrepreneurship. The inaugural ceremony was graced by […] The post 3D in Bangladesh calls at the inaugural ceremony of DIBW 100 designers’ runway appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: “3D in BD — Discovered, Designed & Developed in Bangladesh” Design in Bangladesh Week 2026 officially opened at the United Convention Centre, Dhaka, bringing 100 Bangladeshi designers onto one collective platform and runway to showcase the country’s growing capacity in design, creativity, craftsmanship, innovation, product development and creative entrepreneurship. The inaugural ceremony was graced by Dr. S. M. Ziauddin Hyder, Special Assistant to the Honorable Prime Minister on Health Affairs, with the status of State Minister, as Chief Guest. In his address, Dr. Hyder welcomed the participation and work of 100 designers and encouraged the Design in Bangladesh platform to continue developing as a collaborative creative hub connecting talent, heritage, enterprise, industry and opportunity. He also highlighted the relevance of “One Village, One Product” and the 3D in BD vision — Discovered, Designed & Developed in Bangladesh — as approaches that can help create greater value from Bangladesh’s own creative capacity. Design in Bangladesh Week positions design as an important contributor to Bangladesh’s creative economy — connecting original ideas and cultural knowledge with research, product development, manufacturing, branding, entrepreneurship and market access. The initiative seeks to complement the country’s wider ambition to strengthen innovation, value addition and creative enterprise by building stronger connections between creative talent and Bangladesh’s established production ecosystem. 100 DESIGNERS — ONE PLATFORM At the heart of the opening was the 100 Designers Showcase and Runway, bringing together 100 creative voices on one shared platform. title: All About AI: Kirti Poonia & Prateek Gupte of Caimera
summary: Caimera's founders on what they believe it takes to turn generative output into material that brands are willing to put in front of customers. The post All About AI: Kirti Poonia & Prateek Gupte of Caimera appeared first on The Interline .
content: Originally released in The Interline’s AI Report 2026 , this executive interview with Caimera is one of a 17-part series that sees The Interline quiz executives from companies who have either introduced new AI solutions or added meaningful new AI capabilities into their existing platforms . For more exclusive interviews, stories and opinions from different industry perspectives, and real survey feedback from voices from every level of fashion, download The AI Report 2026 . We’re observing a big disconnect (in both our own fashion-only data and in wider benchmarks from other sources) between the increasing capability and reliability of AI, in both a general sense and in discrete applications, and the lack of trust that end users place in its outputs. What does trust in your specific applications of AI look like, and how do you achieve and measure it? Kirti Poonia: Successfully taming the powerful chaos of AI into consistent usable consumer facing results for the fashion industry has been Caimera’s USP. We build trust through accuracy. Our Sketch to Image accuracy is the highest in the world. It doesn’t provide many options because it provides 1 absolutely consistent output. When designers see that the output faithfully reflects a product’s print, construction, and seams, not a vague interpretation of it, they start using it. That’s the shift. Our sketch to image results are so accurate that they are being used for consumer facing points of sale as well. Trust, for us, is measured very simply: whether a large brand, extremely critical and focused on quality will put our output in front of their customers? content: BUFT National Entrepreneurship Expo 2026 (3.0) opened on 7 October 2026 at BGMEA University of Fashion & Technology (BUFT), bringing together students, academics, entrepreneurs and industry leaders to promote innovation, entrepreneurship and AI-driven business solutions. Organized by the BUFT Business Club in association with the Faculty of Business Studies (FBS), the two-day expo is being held on 7–8 October under the theme “Empowering the Next Generation with AI: Entrepreneurship, Innovation, and Sustainable Digital Transformation.” The expo aims to equip students with entrepreneurial skills and encourage them to harness AI and emerging technologies for innovative and sustainable ventures. title: EverDye gains industry recognition
title_ko: EverDye, 업계 인정 획득

Founded in 2021, EverDye has developed a pigment dyeing process designed to operate at room temperature while consuming significantly less energy than conventional textile dyeing. content: French textile technology start-up EverDye has secured ZDHC certification and been selected for a CEMATEX Start-Up Grant, providing further industry recognition for its low-energy, bio-based approach to textile dyeing. Founded in 2021, EverDye has developed a pigment dyeing process designed to operate at room temperature while consuming significantly less energy than conventional textile dyeing. The company says its technology can reduce CO2 emissions by 90% and cut energy consumption eightfold compared with traditional processes. The company is led by founder Dr Amira Erokh, a materials chemist who has developed an approach based on bio-based pigments and green chemistry. EverDye’s ZDHC certification confirms that its chemical product complies with the ZDHC Manufacturing Restricted Substances List (MRSL). The Zero Discharge of Hazardous Chemicals initiative works globally to support the elimination of hazardous chemicals from textile, apparel, leather and footwear manufacturing. According to EverDye, the certification validates its approach to using bio-based pigments while limiting chemical residues during processing. “The ZDHC certification confirms that it is possible to transform the dyeing process without compromising on chemical control,” said Erokh. “At EverDye, we want to drive a profound shift in the industry towards a more responsible model, starting with dyeing. This recognition gives brands and manufacturers a concrete guarantee for partnering with us.” EverDye’s technology uses a chemistry based on affinity, with pigments rapidly anchoring to fibres. This enables dyeing to take place quickly and at room temperature, with the company claiming reduced chemical residues, lower water and energy consumption and rich, durable colours. content: Shima Seiki will showcase its latest computerised flat knitting and digital design technologies at IGATEX Pakistan 2026, taking place from 15-18 October at Expo Centre Lahore. The Japanese knitting technology specialist will exhibit together with its Pakistani representative, Almurtaza Machinery Co., presenting machinery, 3D design software and online services aimed at supporting efficient and sustainable knitwear production. Among the machinery on display will be the N.SSR112 V14G computerised flat knitting machine. Designed to combine productivity with cost performance, the machine incorporates Shima Seiki technologies including the R2CARRIAGE system for faster carriage returns, movable sinkers, DSCS Digital Stitch Control System, stitch presser and takedown comb. © Shima Seiki Also featured will be the N.SSR072 C16G, a machine based on the N.SSR112 platform and developed specifically for efficient production of shaped jacquard collars from computer-generated designs. Shima Seiki says both machines combine Japanese manufacturing quality and reliability with productivity and ease of operation. © Shima Seiki Digital product development will form another major part of the company’s presentation in Lahore. Demonstrations will include the SDS-ONE APEX4 3D design system and subscription-based APEXFiz Design software, which support fashion development from initial planning and design through to realistic fabric simulation and 3D virtual sampling. Shima Seiki says virtual sampling can replace physical prototypes with accurate digital versions, reducing development time, costs and material consumption. summary: Global cotton consumption is projected to exceed production in the 2026/27 season as production, trade, and ending stocks decline modestly, according to the latest estimates from the International Cotton Advisory Committee (ICAC). The decline in production is largely attributed to reduced cotton area across most major producing countries. Global cotton production is projected at approximately […] The post Global Cotton Consumption Trending Up, Production Trending Down for 2026/27 Season appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Global cotton consumption is projected to exceed production in the 2026/27 season as production, trade, and ending stocks decline modestly, according to the latest estimates from the International Cotton Advisory Committee (ICAC). The decline in production is largely attributed to reduced cotton area across most major producing countries. Global cotton production is projected at approximately 25.94 million tonnes in 2026/27, down 3.8% from 26.98 million tonnes in 2025/26. Consumption, meanwhile, is expected to increase by approximately 1.1%, from 25.85 million tonnes to 26.14 million tonnes. The projections represent a notable shift in the global cotton balance. In 2025/26, production is estimated to exceed consumption by approximately 1.13 million tonnes. In 2026/27, that relationship is projected to reverse, with consumption exceeding production by approximately 201,000 tonnes. Global Cotton Trade Projected to Ease World cotton exports are projected to decline modestly in 2026/27, from approximately 9.87 million tonnes to 9.70 million tonnes, a decrease of about 1.7%. The projected decline comes despite slightly higher global cotton consumption, highlighting a market in which overall mill use is expected to strengthen even as international trade volumes ease. Ending Stocks Expected to Decline Global ending stocks also are projected to decrease, from approximately 17.70 million tonnes in 2025/26 to 17.50 million tonnes in 2026/27, a decline of about 1.1%. The combination of lower production, slightly higher consumption, and declining ending stocks points to a somewhat tighter global cotton balance in the coming season. Every major investment must therefore take the climate conditions of the […] The post Climate policies and plans must translate into effective projects, financing and measurable results: Environment Minister appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Abdul Awal Mintoo emphasized the need to translate national climate policies and plans into coordinated programmes, quality projects, appropriate financing and measurable results. He said that today’s development decisions would shape climate risks for decades to come. Every major investment must therefore take the climate conditions of the relevant area into account. The Minister made these remarks as the chief guest at the opening ceremony of the two-day Bangladesh Climate Development Partnership (BCDP) Knowledge Conference 2026 at the Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel in Dhaka today, Wednesday. On the occasion, he launched the BCDP Web Portal. Through real-time project monitoring, the digital portal will help manage information on climate-related projects and investments, enhance transparency and improve processes for developing domestic and international climate finance pipelines. The Minister said that adaptation investments often deliver significant public benefits even when they do not generate direct revenue. Climate financing arrangements must reflect Bangladesh’s development priorities and fiscal capacity. He also called for private investment in clean energy and sustainable infrastructure. Emphasizing the importance of drawing on local communities’ experience in planning, the Minister said that women, young people, persons with disabilities and marginalized communities must have meaningful opportunities to participate in project design, implementation and monitoring. Alongside effective institutions, sound investment decisions and transparent use of resources, Bangladesh would continue to call for international support and climate justice in addressing adaptation and climate-related loss and damage. title: Parkdale acquires CiCLO to advance lower-persistence synthetic fibers
title_ko: Parkdale은 CiCLO를 인수하여 저잔류성 합성 섬유를 발전시킵니다.
summary: Parkdale Advanced Materials has acquired full ownership of CiCLO technology, a patented additive designed to reduce the environmental persistence of microplastic fibers. Figure: Parkdale acquires CiC...
content: Parkdale Advanced Materials has acquired full ownership of CiCLO technology, a patented additive designed to reduce the environmental persistence of microplastic fibers. Figure: Parkdale acquires CiCLO to advance lower-persistence synthetic fibers. CiCLO technology is integrated into polyester and nylon during the extrusion or spinning process. The acquisition gives Parkdale full control of the technology and expands its polymer and fiber portfolio. According to Knitting Trade Journal, the technology is intended to support further development in knitted textiles and related industrial markets. CiCLO is designed for use in synthetic fibers, including polyester and nylon. These fibers can shed microfibres during textile use and washing. The technology aims to make these fibers less persistent in the environment. The acquisition also allows Parkdale to further develop CiCLO technology for textile and industrial applications. It could support the company’s work on synthetic fiber solutions with lower environmental persistence. Parkdale Advanced Materials is a subsidiary of Parkdale, a textile and fiber producer. The company’s expanded technology portfolio now includes full ownership of the patented CiCLO additive. The deal reflects growing industry interest in technologies that can address the environmental impact of synthetic fibers while maintaining their use in textile applications.

content: JBCCI organized its 21st Annual General Meeting (AGM), at Hotel Lakeshore. JBCCI’s General members, Board members and Distinguished guests and media professionals, a turnout of nearly 240 guests from different organizations joined in this Program. Ms. Tahera Ahsan, Executive Director, JBCCI moderated the program. Mr. Tareq Rafi Bhuiyan (Jun), President, JBCCI delivered his welcoming remarks and illustrated JBCCI’s role in recent times for developing bilateral trade relations between Japan and Bangladesh further. In his remarks, Mr. Tareq Rafi Bhuiyan (Jun), President of JBCCI, highlighted the longstanding trust and growing economic partnership between Bangladesh and Japan, noting that JBCCI has served as an important bridge between the two business communities since its establishment in 2004. He described the signing of the Japan–Bangladesh Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) as a historic milestone and stressed the importance of its timely ratification, effective implementation, and business readiness to fully utilize the opportunities it offers. He also emphasized the need for a predictable and investor-friendly business environment, continued policy advocacy, stronger business connectivity, and greater participation of women in business. Referring to major Japan-supported infrastructure projects, he underscored their importance in advancing Bangladesh’s economic development. As he concluded his term as President, he expressed gratitude to the Embassy of Japan, JETRO, JICA, JCIAD, the JBCCI Board, Secretariat and members, and conveyed his confidence that the incoming leadership would further strengthen trade, investment and friendship between Bangladesh and Japan. title: Virgin polyester rises 7%, global fiber output hits 139m tons
title_ko: 버진 폴리에스터 가격 7% 상승, 전 세계 섬유 생산량 1억 3900만 톤 기록
summary: Global textile fiber production reached a record 139 million tons in 2025, up from 132 million tons a year earlier, with growth again driven largely by virgin fossil-based fibers, according to Textil...
content: Global textile fiber production reached a record 139 million tons in 2025, up from 132 million tons a year earlier, with growth again driven largely by virgin fossil-based fibers, according to Textile Exchange’s Materials Market Report 2026 . Virgin fossil-based fiber production rose from 81 million tons in 2024 to 86 million tons in 2025. Polyester remained the world’s dominant fiber. Production increased from 77.7 million tons to 82.5 million tons, maintaining a 59% share of global fiber output. Of that volume, 72.8 million tons, or 88%, was virgin fossil-based polyester. The figures underline a widening gap between the textile industry’s circularity ambitions and actual fiber production trends. While brands and manufacturers are increasingly setting recycled-material and lower-impact sourcing targets, the absolute volume of virgin polyester continues to grow. Recycled polyester production increased only modestly, from about 9.4 million tons in 2024 to 9.7 million tons in 2025. Around 97% still came from plastic bottles, rather than discarded textiles. Textile-to-textile recycled fiber production across all fiber types accounted for just 0.76% of global fiber output in 2025, up only marginally from 0.61% in 2021. This is important because bottle-based recycled polyester can reduce reliance on virgin fossil feedstock, but it does not by itself create a closed-loop textile system. The industry’s longer-term circularity challenge is therefore not simply to increase recycled polyester volumes, but to scale fiber-to-fiber recycling capable of turning textile waste back into textile raw material. title: First mountain biking range from Ortovox
title_ko: Ortovox의 최초 산악자전거 코스
summary: The new Sequence Series mountain biking collection from German brand Ortovox is based on 100% textile-to-textile recycled polyester, marking a significant departure for a company that has built much of its technical apparel identity around the advanced performance properties of wool. Synthetic fibres used in high-intensity sportswear, however, can retain sweat-related odours, prompting Ortovox to […] The post First mountain biking range from Ortovox appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: The new Sequence Series mountain biking collection from German brand Ortovox is based on 100% textile-to-textile recycled polyester, marking a significant departure for a company that has built much of its technical apparel identity around the advanced performance properties of wool. Synthetic fibres used in high-intensity sportswear, however, can retain sweat-related odours, prompting Ortovox to incorporate Microban International’s Scentry Revive odour-capture technology directly into the fabric during manufacture. Rather than relying on an antimicrobial mechanism, the technology captures and neutralises odour molecules before they become established in the fabric. Microban says its effectiveness is retained for up to 50 domestic washes. For Ortovox, the development provides a way of combining textile-to-textile recycled polyester with the performance requirements of clothing intended for prolonged trail riding. Reducing persistent odours can potentially also reduce the frequency with which garments need to be washed, potentially extending garment life. Scentry Revive has Eco Passport by Oeko-Tex and bluesign certification and does not require biocidal registration. Founded in 1980 and headquartered in Taufkirchen near Munich, Ortovox has traditionally concentrated on ski touring, freeriding, alpine climbing and high-alpine activities, with mountain biking being added to its portfolio for the first time in summer 2026. Microban International is headquartered in North Carolina and supplies antimicrobial and odour-control technologies for consumer, textile, industrial and medical applications. www.ortovox.com The post First mountain biking range from Ortovox appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

title: Noakhali gas well shows potential to add 7mmcf daily to national grid
summary: A new gas discovery in Noakhali has opened the prospect of additional domestic gas supply to Bangladesh’s national grid. Although the size and commercial potential of the find will depend on the resul...
content: A new gas discovery in Noakhali has opened the prospect of additional domestic gas supply to Bangladesh’s national grid. Although the size and commercial potential of the find will depend on the results of an ongoing production test. Gas was discovered at the Sundalpur-4 Appraisal cum Development Well in Bar Charigaon village of Nabipur Union under Senbag upazila. Project Director Md. Mozammel Haque confirmed the discovery on Wednesday (October 7), saying a Drill Stem Test (DST) is now underway. Courtesy: Collected The test is expected to take another four to five days and will determine the well’s reserve and recoverable gas volume. Preliminary estimates suggest the well could produce around 7 million cubic feet of gas per day for the national grid. The potential production rate makes the discovery significant for Bangladesh’s domestic gas supply, but the actual contribution of the well cannot be assessed until the DST establishes its sustainable production capacity and recoverable reserves. The gas presence was formally confirmed on 06 October after drilling was completed and a flame was ignited at the pipehead. Drilling of the well began on July 28 under Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company Limited (BAPEX). BAPEX sources said the well was drilled to a depth of 1,578 meters using directional drilling and Measurement While Drilling (MWD) technology. Gas was encountered at depths of 1,420 to 1,460 meters. The location of the new discovery also extends the operational significance of the Sundalpur gas structure. Three previous wells—Sundalpur-1, Sundalpur-2 and Sundalpur-3—were drilled in Sirajpur of Companiganj upazila. title: BOGE: Engineering the Future of Efficient, Connected Compressed-Air Solutions
title_ko: BOGE: 효율적이고 연결된 압축 공기 솔루션의 미래 엔지니어링
summary: By K. Gopalakrishnan Compressed air is an essential but often overlooked component of modern industrial production, with its efficiency, reliability and quality having a direct bearing on productivity and operating… The post BOGE: Engineering the Future of Efficient, Connected Compressed-Air Solutions appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: By K. Gopalakrishnan Compressed air is an essential but often overlooked component of modern industrial production, with its efficiency, reliability and quality having a direct bearing on productivity and operating costs. As manufacturers face growing pressure to reduce energy consumption, improve sustainability and adopt smarter production systems, compressed-air technology is increasingly moving from a utility function to a strategic element of plant efficiency. Mr. Nalin Amunugama, General Manager, BOGE Asia Pacific Against this backdrop, BOGE has evolved from a traditional compressor manufacturer into a provider of integrated compressed-air and gas solutions, combining compressor technologies with air treatment, intelligent controls, heat recovery, digital monitoring and gas-generation systems. With a global presence spanning more than 120 countries, the company is increasingly focused on application-specific solutions that optimise the complete compressed-air system rather than individual equipment alone. Technology, energy efficiency and digitalisation are at the heart of this evolution. BOGE is advancing oil-free compression, high-efficiency systems, intelligent controls and connected solutions that enable manufacturers to monitor performance, optimise energy consumption and move towards more predictive maintenance. In the textile industry, where compressed air is integral to processes ranging from spinning and weaving to pneumatic controls and material handling, these capabilities can have a direct impact on productivity, quality and manufacturing costs. Asia Pacific is a particularly important growth region for BOGE, with the company seeing opportunities across rapidly expanding manufacturing sectors, including textiles. title: Fashion for Good launches the Cotton Reloop Matrix Project
title_ko: Fashion for Good은 Cotton Reloop Matrix 프로젝트를 시작합니다.
summary: Fashion for Good announces the launch of the Cotton Reloop Matrix Project, a cross-industry initiative that will map and physically validate the quality of commercially available recycled cotton yarns against… The post Fashion for Good launches the Cotton Reloop Matrix Project appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: Fashion for Good announces the launch of the Cotton Reloop Matrix Project, a cross-industry initiative that will map and physically validate the quality of commercially available recycled cotton yarns against brand specifications, giving the industry a data-backed overview of how quality, price, and recycled content intersect. The project is convened with Fashion for Good partners Arvind, BESTSELLER, C&A, Interloop, Reformation, and Shahi, together with ecosystem partner Uster. Cotton accounts for 19% of global fibre production and a core part of the material mix. Although alternative recycling pathways exist to utilise cotton-rich textile waste feedstock, they do not make a cotton output. Therefore, mechanical recycling is a crucial pathway to utilise waste and create recycled cotton yarns and fabrics. Through the mechanical recycling process, textile waste is shredded and re-opened into loose fibres that can be respun into yarn. However, shredding shortens and weakens the fibres, so only 45 to 50% of the input survives as usable material . The rest is lost as short fibres and processing waste, and because the surviving fibres are shorter than virgin cotton, spinners can only blend a limited share back into new yarn. In practice, that caps most yarns at around 10% recycled content: any higher and the fabric isn’t durable enough for commercial use. While recyclers have available capacities, integrating a meaningful percentage of recycled cotton remains complex for brands navigating trade-offs around quality and price. Testing happens in isolation, with recyclers and brands working from separate data sets, and no shared reference comparison to close the gap between them. title: Neumühle takes monomaterial design down to the thread
title_ko: Neumühle는 단일 소재 디자인을 스레드까지 가져왔습니다.
summary: Zurich, Switzerland-based clothing label Neumühle has extended its monomaterial approach with a new hoodie made entirely from cotton, including the sewing thread, and with no elastane incorporated into its construction. The Circular Mono Hoodie has been designed with eventual textile-to-textile recycling in mind, addressing one of the persistent obstacles to recovering fibres from garments – […] The post Neumühle takes monomaterial design down to the thread appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Zurich, Switzerland-based clothing label Neumühle has extended its monomaterial approach with a new hoodie made entirely from cotton, including the sewing thread, and with no elastane incorporated into its construction. The Circular Mono Hoodie has been designed with eventual textile-to-textile recycling in mind, addressing one of the persistent obstacles to recovering fibres from garments – the presence of multiple materials within a single product. Its heavyweight fabric is made from 100% organic cotton, while the sewing thread is also cotton and Cradle to Cradle Certified. By eliminating elastane, Neumühle avoids introducing an additional fibre that would subsequently have to be separated or accommodated during recycling. The approach reflects growing attention to the relationship between garment design and the practicalities of fibre-to-fibre recycling. Neumühle points to a 2026 study from Wageningen University and Research examining discarded textiles in the Dutch clothing system, which found that 61% consisted of material blends. The researchers concluded that monomaterial products, or garments incorporating components that can easily be separated, are considerably better suited to efficient, high-quality textile-to-textile recycling. The Circular Mono Hoodie is consequently intended to address end-of-life requirements at the initial material-selection and design stages rather than attempting to deal with incompatible components once a garment enters the waste stream. content: A first-of-its-kind collaboration transforms four distinctive LUX body care and their signature fragrances into four fashion muses through the creative lens of Blucheez. Dhaka, Bangladesh | October 2026 — When a body wash experience becomes a fragrance, and fragrance becomes fashion, a new kind of story begins. This season, Blucheez and LUX, a renowned beauty and personal care brand from the Unilever portfolio, come together for a distinctive creative collaboration that brings the worlds of body care, fragrance, fashion and beauty into one immersive expression. Introducing “Garden of Wonders”, the LUX × BLUCHEEZ Limited-Edition Collection. Inspired by four distinctive LUX body washes and their captivating fragrances, the collection interprets each scent through the language of fashion, translating its essence into colour, texture, silhouette and character. Rather than simply reflecting the fragrances, Blucheez has imagined each one as an individual muse, complete with its own personality, visual identity and story. Four Scents. Four Muses. Four Worlds. At the heart of Garden of Wonders is the idea that a body wash can be more than part of a daily beauty ritual. Its fragrance can evoke a mood, inspire a feeling and become an expression of personality. Through the Blucheez creative lens, each LUX fragrance takes on a new form. Every silhouette becomes an expression of its muse, creating a collection where the sensory world of LUX body care meets the visual and expressive language of fashion. content: PHOENIX — October 6, 2026 — At the upcoming Fall High Point Market, Purecare will launch the Refreshing Puffed pillow collection featuring TENCEL Lyocell and blended Identically Down fiber fill options. The new pillow line expands the wellness-focused bedding brand’s growing line of domestically made pillows, filled and finished at its Phoenix, Arizona campus. Purecare Refreshing Puffed Pillow collection Purecare’s addition of the Refreshing Puffed pillow collection builds on the brand’s successful TENCEL Lyocell sheet and mattress protector programs, which have been a staple in its lineup for well over a decade. The new Refreshing Puffed pillows include a TENCEL Lyocell blended cover and two blended fill options. “Domestic pillow production has been a true gamechanger for Purecare,” said Sarah Bergman, chief marketing officer, Purecare. “We’re designing custom, ready-to-ship pillow programs for retailers around the country because we can control the quality, inject innovation and hit the price points that our retailers need.” The Refreshing Puffed line offers a choice of adjustable fills. The option with blended cooling shredded foam and Identically Down fiber is offered at $79.97 MSRP and the blended shredded latex and Identically Down fiber fill at $99.97 MSRP, with additional fill options available upon request. title: IND HEMP Invests In Premium Fiber Processing Line
title_ko: IND HEMP, 프리미엄 섬유 가공 라인에 투자
summary: FORT BENTON, Mont. — October 1, 2026 — IND HEMP, a producer, processor and supplier of industrial hemp materials in the USA, today announced a significant investment in new fiber processing equipment at its IH Fiber decortication facility in Fort Benton, Montana. The investment adds a secondary processing line, featuring multiple fiber refining technologies to […]
content: FORT BENTON, Mont. — October 1, 2026 — IND HEMP, a producer, processor and supplier of industrial hemp materials in the USA, today announced a significant investment in new fiber processing equipment at its IH Fiber decortication facility in Fort Benton, Montana. The investment adds a secondary processing line, featuring multiple fiber refining technologies to perform opening, cleaning and cottonizing, that brings IND HEMP’s hemp fiber to a ready-to-spin quality directly at the source. Yarn is the foundation from which nearly every fabric application is built. Once hemp fiber is spun into yarn, it can be woven or knit into a wide range of end products, from garments and home goods to technical fabrics such as composites. Historically, reaching that spinnable quality has required additional refining beyond standard decortication, work that has fallen to third-party processors, or to the spinners themselves, upgrading standard decorticated technical fiber before it can run on their equipment. The commissioning of IND HEMP’s new processing line brings that refining capability in-house, at the fiber’s source. “Consumers are increasingly looking for natural materials and more transparent supply chains, and brands are moving quickly to try to meet that demand. Hemp is an incredible plant-based solution, but until now the U.S. hasn’t been capable of consistently delivering the quality and scale the global textile industry requires,” explains IND HEMP CEO Morgan Tweet. “By supplying ready-to-spin fiber directly from Montana, we’re removing one of the biggest barriers for manufacturers wanting to work with hemp. title: CPM Names Jeremy Patten Chief Executive Office
summary: BLAINE, Minn. — October 2, 2026 — CPM, a global provider of process equipment, engineered technologies and aftermarket support, announced today that Jeremy Patten has joined the company as Chief Executive Officer. Patten brings more than 20 years of leadership experience across global industrial, manufacturing and technology-driven businesses. Most recently, he served as President of […]
content: BLAINE, Minn. — October 2, 2026 — CPM, a global provider of process equipment, engineered technologies and aftermarket support, announced today that Jeremy Patten has joined the company as Chief Executive Officer. Jeremy Patten Patten brings more than 20 years of leadership experience across global industrial, manufacturing and technology-driven businesses. Most recently, he served as President of Modine’s Performance Technologies segment. Prior to Modine, he spent more than eight years with ATS Corporation, including serving as President of its Packaging and Food Technology Group. Earlier in his career, Patten held leadership roles with IDEX Corporation and Danaher Corporation. “Jeremy brings the combination of operational leadership, commercial experience and focus on execution that makes him well suited to lead CPM,” said Simon Peckham, Chief Executive of Rosebank Industries. “CPM has strong market positions, longstanding customer relationships and significant opportunities for growth. We are pleased to have Jeremy leading the business as we invest to build on those strengths, grow the aftermarket and improve performance across the organization.” Patten joins CPM as the company continues to focus on growth, operational improvement and strengthening support for customers throughout the full lifecycle of their equipment. “CPM has strong brands, deep engineering expertise, long-standing customer relationships and a significant global installed base,” said Patten. “What attracted me to CPM is the opportunity to build on those strengths, grow the business and continue improving how we support our customers throughout the lifecycle of their equipment. I’m looking forward to getting to know our people, customers and businesses around the world.” Posted: October 6, 2026 Sour

summary: Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer and Leader of the Opposition in Parliament, Dr. Shafiqur Rahman, held a meeting with leaders of the Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA) to discuss the current challenges and future prospects of the country’s textile industry. The meeting was held on Tuesday afternoon at the official residence of the Leader of the Opposition […] The post Jamaat Leaders Hold Meeting with BTMA Delegation on Textile Sector Challenges appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer and Leader of the Opposition in Parliament, Dr. Shafiqur Rahman, held a meeting with leaders of the Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA) to discuss the current challenges and future prospects of the country’s textile industry. The meeting was held on Tuesday afternoon at the official residence of the Leader of the Opposition at 29 Minto Road in the capital. The discussions focused on several key issues affecting the textile sector, including incentives, gas and electricity supply, challenges following Bangladesh’s graduation from the Least Developed Country (LDC) category, taxes and duties, and various policy-related complexities. Speaking at a press briefing after the meeting, Jamaat Secretary General and former Member of Parliament Mia Golam Parwar said Dr. Shafiqur Rahman emphasized that the opposition does not intend to oppose every government initiative. He said the party wants to play a constructive role by supporting initiatives that serve the public interest while highlighting and opposing policies that are against national interests. According to Mia Golam Parwar, BTMA leaders presented various challenges faced by the textile industry. Dr. Shafiqur Rahman highlighted the importance of ensuring raw materials for export-oriented industries, protecting the capacity of the primary textile sector, increasing local value addition, safeguarding employment, conserving foreign exchange and government revenue, and preventing misuse of bond facilities and illegal imports. He said such balanced and coordinated policies could help strengthen Bangladesh’s primary textile industry, export capacity and overall industrial base. He also assured that the concerns raised by the sector would be brought to Parliament and discussed with the gov

title: BKMEA President Calls on Students to Embrace Integrity, Innovation and Industry-Ready Skills
title_ko: BKMEA 회장, 학생들에게 성실성, 혁신 및 업계에 준비된 기술을 수용할 것을 촉구
summary: BKMEA President Mr. Mohammad Hatem attended the ‘DIU Textile Grand Carnival’, organised by the Department of Textile Engineering of Daffodil International University, as the Chief Guest, where he shared valuable guidance with the students on professional integrity, skills and future opportunities. Addressing the students, he emphasised the importance of honesty, sincerity and dedication in professional […] The post BKMEA President Calls on Students to Embrace Integrity, Innovation and Industry-Ready Skills appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: BKMEA President Mr. Mohammad Hatem attended the ‘DIU Textile Grand Carnival’, organised by the Department of Textile Engineering of Daffodil International University, as the Chief Guest, where he shared valuable guidance with the students on professional integrity, skills and future opportunities. Addressing the students, he emphasised the importance of honesty, sincerity and dedication in professional life. He reminded them that the task they are performing deserves their utmost attention and that they themselves are equally important. Therefore, every responsibility should be carried out with full concentration, commitment and sincerity. He also encouraged students to build their knowledge and skills in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Sustainability, highlighting that the young generation will shape the future of the apparel industry. He further called for extending the internship period for textile students from three months to six months. He mentioned that BKMEA will take initiatives to facilitate internship opportunities across its member factories, enabling students to gain practical industry experience and develop the skills required to become industry-ready professionals. Also present at the event were DIU Vice Chancellor Prof. Dr. Engr. M. R. Kabir, Dean of the Faculty of Engineering Prof. Dr. M. Shamsul Alam, Head of the Department of Textile Engineering Dr. Engr. Tanvir Ahmed Chowdhury, along with faculty members and students. title: Milliken Achieves Cradle To Cradle Certified® Silver Version 5.0 For Global Carpet Portfolio
summary: SPARTANBURG, S.C. — September 30, 2026 — Milliken & Company has achieved Cradle to Cradle Certified® Silver Version 5.0 for its global carpet portfolio, reinforcing the company’s longstanding commitment to material health, product circularity, and sustainability leadership. The certification provides architects, designers, and building owners with independent validation that Milliken products meet rigorous requirements across […]
content: SPARTANBURG, S.C. — September 30, 2026 — Milliken & Company has achieved Cradle to Cradle Certified® Silver Version 5.0 for its global carpet portfolio, reinforcing the company’s longstanding commitment to material health, product circularity, and sustainability leadership. The certification provides architects, designers, and building owners with independent validation that Milliken products meet rigorous requirements across multiple sustainability categories. Cradle to Cradle Certified® is one of the built environment’s most recognized sustainability certifications, evaluating products across areas such as material health, product circularity, clean air and climate protection, water and soil stewardship, and social fairness. Milliken’s certification covers the full scope of these requirements, demonstrating a holistic approach to responsible product design and manufacturing. “For many customers, sustainability information has become increasingly complex,” said Allie Bruski, Vice President, Product Marketing for Milliken’s flooring business. “This certification provides confidence that when they specify Milliken flooring, they are choosing products that have been independently evaluated for material health, circularity, and broader sustainability performance.” The certification also reflects Milliken’s broader legacy of transparency and product stewardship. For decades, the company has invested in helping customers better understand the materials that contribute to healthier, higher-performing spaces. Cradle to Cradle Certified® Silver provides trusted third-party validation of that commitment. content: Wendler Interlining Bangladesh Limited. organised a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) programme titled ‘Together for Tomorrow’ at Obhizatrik School, which is managed by the charity organisation, Obhizatrik Foundation. This effort reflects Wendler’s dedication to sustainability and local support, aiming to supply essential goods to disadvantaged students. Wendler Inside is a German-based global company that assists the textile supply chain through interlining, tapes, and accessories. It has operated worldwide for more than 180 years. Established in 2010, Obhizatrik Foundation is a government-registered non-profit organization in Bangladesh and Portugal. It seeks lasting change for the underprivileged by strengthening education, healthcare, nutrition, and financial prospects. In a sincere ceremony, Wendler provided school bags and meals to the students. Dr Gerhart Wendler, Chairman of Wendler Interlining Group, then visited the classrooms and spoke with students, encouraging environmental awareness and well-being. Senior management joined him to hand out snacks and essential stationery to everyone. Dr Gerhart Wendler personally distributed the gifts to the eager students. The Wendler’s Support team, including Head of Sales and Marketing Aman Hossain, Operations Director Ashief Khan, and GM Asia Kanat Altunbas, attended the occasion along with other colleagues. Founder-President of OBHIZATRIK, Mr Ahmed Imtiaz Jami, thanked Wendler Interlining Bangladesh for its generosity. title_ko: Amin & Jahan Corporation Ltd.는 SGS Bangladesh를 만나 섬유 및 가죽 분야의 ZDHC Academy 교육을 발전시킵니다.
summary: To accelerate sustainable manufacturing, enhance environmental compliance, and improve resource efficiency across Bangladesh’s industrial value chains, Amin & Jahan Corporation Limited (A&J) a...
content: To accelerate sustainable manufacturing, enhance environmental compliance, and improve resource efficiency across Bangladesh’s industrial value chains, Amin & Jahan Corporation Limited (A&J) and SGS Bangladesh Ltd. held a strategic coordination meeting at their Karwan Bazar Office. The meeting focused on establishing a collaborative framework to roll out globally accredited ZDHC Academy Training programs, specifically addressing Chemical Management and Wastewater Management across the textile, apparel, leather, and tannery manufacturing sectors in Bangladesh. Figure: Officials from SGS Bangladesh Ltd. and Amin and Jahan Corporation Ltd. following the strategic planning session for ZDHC Academy Training. Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) to join this program: https://bit.ly/zdhc-bd During the discussion, both organizations agreed on a phased implementation structure tailored to regional supply chain requirements. Participating facilities will first undergo comprehensive Chemical Management modules, followed by advanced Wastewater Management training once core chemical stewardship practices are embedded on the factory floor. The curriculum will also incorporate sector-specific adaptations for textile mills and leather tanneries, ensuring targeted alignment with the ZDHC Roadmap to Zero guidelines, discharge standards, and international compliance benchmarks. To maximize shop-floor absorption while maintaining international technical rigor, the interactive capacity-building initiative will blend global course materials with localized, bilingual delivery. SGS Bangladesh will also conduct baseline technical assessments to identify common operational bottlenecks across facilities prior to program execution. title: Bangladesh Launches Initiative to Advance Textile Traceability and Decarbonization
title_ko: Bangladesh, 섬유 추적성 및 탈탄소화 발전을 위한 이니셔티브 시작
summary: Solidaridad Asia, in partnership with the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Bangladesh, the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO), Dutch retail brands, technology innovators and Bangladesh’s apparel industry bodies, has officially launched a 2.5-year initiative titled “Circular Textiles Bangladesh: Advancing Traceability and Decarbonization.” The initiative aims to support Bangladesh’s textile and apparel sector in […] The post Bangladesh Launches Initiative to Advance Textile Traceability and Decarbonization appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Solidaridad Asia, in partnership with the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Bangladesh, the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO), Dutch retail brands, technology innovators and Bangladesh’s apparel industry bodies, has officially launched a 2.5-year initiative titled “Circular Textiles Bangladesh: Advancing Traceability and Decarbonization.” Photo: Guests, speakers, industry leaders, brand representatives, technology partners and stakeholders pose for a group photograph at the launch of “Circular Textiles Bangladesh: Advancing Traceability and Decarbonization”. The initiative aims to support Bangladesh’s textile and apparel sector in responding to emerging global sustainability and regulatory requirements, particularly those linked to the European Union market. It will focus on practical solutions for product-level traceability, carbon data, transparency and decarbonization across textile and apparel supply chains. The initiative brings together Dutch retailers Zeeman, Wibra and XD Connects, technology providers Aware, tex.tracer, OneTrueValue and Colubris, and industry bodies BGMEA and BKMEA. It will work with manufacturers to test practical solutions around supply chain traceability, circularity, decarbonization and sustainability data. The initiative brings together Dutch retail brands including Zeeman, Wibra and XD Connects; technology innovators Aware, tex.tracer, OneTrueValue and Colubris; and industry organizations including BGMEA and BKMEA. The launch comes as global regulations are increasingly shifting from traditional factory-level compliance toward verified product-level information. content: SHANGHAI — October 6, 2026 — Yarn Expo Spring will welcome the global yarn and fibre industry back to the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai) from 10 – 12 March 2027. The upcoming fair follows its strongest edition to date, held in March this year, when over 600 exhibitors from 12 countries and regions connected with more than 25,000 visitors from 113 countries and regions. The record turnout reaffirmed the fair’s role as a key venue for sourcing, innovation and industry exchange. Returning alongside Intertextile Shanghai Apparel Fabrics – Spring Edition, Intertextile Shanghai Home Textiles – Spring Edition, CHIC and PH Value, the comprehensive yarn and fibre trade fair will create further opportunities for the textile value chain to connect around changing material and sourcing priorities. Prior to the fair, Ms Wilmet Shea, General Manager of Messe Frankfurt (HK) Ltd, commented: “In a changing economic landscape, last year’s record participation showed how important it is for the yarn and fibre industry to meet in Shanghai, exchange ideas and understand what the market needs next. In March, suppliers will have the opportunity to present their latest developments to buyers from apparel, home textiles, knitting and related sectors, discuss requirements and build business relationships for the long term.” Yarn and fibre markets evolve with changing sourcing needs As the yarn, fibre and thread market expands towards a projected USD 182.7 billion by 2032, Asia-Pacific remains central to spinning, filament and textile production, as well as downstream demand. China’s integrated fibre, yarn, textile and equipment segments further strengthen Shanghai’s role as a location for industry exchange. content: By K. Gopalakrishnan Major investment cycle spans spinning, weaving, processing, technical textiles, garments and green energy as Vardhman positions itself for the next phase of India’s textile growth For more than six decades, Vardhman Textiles has grown alongside India’s textile industry, building one of the country’s most extensive vertically integrated textile manufacturing platforms. Today, as global sourcing patterns undergo a structural shift and India strengthens its position as a preferred textile and apparel sourcing destination, the company is embarking on one of the most significant investment cycles in its recent history. Suchita Oswal Jain, Vice-Chairman and Joint Managing Director of Vardhman Textiles Vardhman has committed approximately ₹3,660 crore to a broad-based growth and modernisation programme, covering spinning and fabric, technical textiles, fabric processing, garment manufacturing and green-energy infrastructure. Rather than being a conventional capacity expansion programme, the investment is designed to move the company further up the textile value chain, improve productivity and margins, strengthen sustainability credentials and create a more resilient business model. The scale and breadth of the programme underline Vardhman’s confidence in the long-term prospects of the Indian textile industry. The company believes that global supply chains are being redrawn as brands and retailers diversify sourcing away from concentrated geographies and increasingly seek large, compliant and technologically capable manufacturing partners. title: Results Of The 40th ITMF Global Textile Industry Survey : Slight Improvement, But The Textile Industry Remains Under Pressure
summary: ZÜRICH, Switzerland — October 6, 2026 — The 40th ITMF Global Textile Industry Survey (GTIS), conducted from 21 to 29 September 2026, shows a slight improvement in the global business situation, to -23pp, well above the November 2023 low of -46pp. Conditions nevertheless remain weak, in what has become a new normal of high uncertainty. content: ZÜRICH, Switzerland — October 6, 2026 — The 40th ITMF Global Textile Industry Survey (GTIS), conducted from 21 to 29 September 2026, shows a slight improvement in the global business situation, to -23pp, well above the November 2023 low of -46pp. Conditions nevertheless remain weak, in what has become a new normal of high uncertainty. Only South Asia (+13pp) and Africa (+9pp) are positive, while Europe (-36pp), South America (-44pp) and North & Central America (-56pp) report the weakest conditions. Along the value chain, the two ends are doing better than the middle. Fibre producers (+17pp) are the only positive segment, while spinners (-33pp) and finishers (-42pp) lag. Textile machinery manufacturers (-35pp) continue to suffer from companies’ reluctance to invest. Business expectations for the next six months improved to +19pp, in sharp contrast to the current situation. However, 46% of participants expect no change, a sign that the optimism rests more on hope than on concrete signals. Africa (+59pp) is by far the most optimistic region, while East Asia (-20pp) and Southeast Asia (-6pp) remain pessimistic. Fibre producers (+67pp) are the most confident segment. Order intake edged up to -24pp but remains weak, and South America has fallen to a record low of -69pp. Rising costs and inflation make a significant recovery in the coming months unlikely. The global order backlog shortened slightly to 2.3 months, within the range of 2 to 2.5 months it has held since mid-2023, as most companies work on confirmed orders only. Capacity utilisation rose to 71%, above the November 2023 record low of 68% but still well below the levels above 80% seen before late 2022. title: European textiles demand fair competition
summary: Europe’s textile and clothing industry is calling for fairer competition, stronger support for recycling and measures that ensure the costs of sustainability are shared by all companies selling into the European market. Industry representatives took their case to the European Parliament in Brussels at the event Making Circular Textiles Work in Europe: Transparency, Recycling, and […] The post European textiles demand fair competition appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Europe’s textile and clothing industry is calling for fairer competition, stronger support for recycling and measures that ensure the costs of sustainability are shared by all companies selling into the European market. Industry representatives took their case to the European Parliament in Brussels at the event Making Circular Textiles Work in Europe: Transparency, Recycling, and Industrial Competitiveness, held on 30 September. César Araújo, president of Portugal’s National Association of Clothing, Apparel and Fashion Industries (ANIVEC), argued that the recently announced €2 handling fee on small parcels entering the EU from non-EU countries is insufficient. He said a fee of €10 per parcel would provide a fairer basis for competition and help finance the resources required to inspect rapidly growing volumes of e-commerce shipments. According to Araújo, small parcels entering the EU increased from around 2.7 billion in 2023 to 4.1 billion in 2024 and are expected to approach six billion in 2025. He said the former de minimis system had effectively become a gateway into the European market for e-commerce, particularly from Asian platforms. “This is not about duties. This is about fair competition, product safety, taxation and consumer protection,” Araújo said. He also called for imports and the impact of the EU’s Generalised Scheme of Preferences to be monitored closely, allowing policymakers to respond rapidly when market imbalances emerge. The Brussels debate was organised by CENIT – Textile Intelligence Centre under the Lusitano Project, with the support of ANIVEC and MEPs Paulo Cunha and Bruno Gonçalves. title: US-Grown Hemp Meets Supima
title_ko: 미국산 대마와 수피마의 만남
summary: Hemp is steadily moving from a sustainability-led niche towards a commercially viable fibre for mainstream textile manufacturing, and Heartland USA is seeking to accelerate this transition through scalable fibre solutions… The post US-Grown Hemp Meets Supima appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: Hemp is steadily moving from a sustainability-led niche towards a commercially viable fibre for mainstream textile manufacturing, and Heartland USA is seeking to accelerate this transition through scalable fibre solutions and strategic blends. Its recent innovation combining US-grown Imperium hemp fibre with Supima® cotton demonstrates the potential to integrate hemp into commercial spinning systems while creating premium textile possibilities around performance, natural fibres and a distinctive “Grown in America” proposition. According to Mr. Amey Padma, Head – India Business, Heartland USA, the next phase of hemp adoption will depend on consistent fibre quality, reliable supply, technical compatibility and, ultimately, commercial economics. Hemp is gaining renewed attention as textile manufacturers and global brands search for natural fibre alternatives that can deliver sustainability as well as commercially relevant performance. For Heartland USA, the opportunity extends beyond positioning hemp as another sustainable fibre. The company is focused on making hemp compatible with existing textile manufacturing infrastructure and developing commercially viable fibre blends for apparel and home textiles. Mr. Amey Padma, Head – India Business, Heartland USA According to Mr. Amey Padmas, the global hemp market is gradually moving “from niche to industrial”, particularly through applications involving cotton, lyocell and other fibre blends. However, he believes that mainstream adoption will ultimately depend on three factors: consistency, economics and supply reliability. “Sustainability gets attention; performance and economics drive adoption,” says Padma. content: By K. Gopalakrishnan Three decades after entering India, LAPP has made the country its second-largest market globally and its biggest investment base in Asia. With India emerging as a major manufacturing hub, the company is expanding local production, developing application-specific solutions and investing in technology, sustainability and talent to drive its next phase of growth. When LAPP established its presence in India 30 years ago, many European companies were looking primarily towards China and other Asian markets. LAPP, however, chose to make a long-term bet on India. Three decades later, that decision has paid off handsomely. Matthias Lapp, CEO, LAPP Group India is now LAPP’s second-largest market globally, after Germany, and its largest investment destination in Asia. The company’s growing commitment is reflected in the expansion of its Bhopal manufacturing facility, which is set to become LAPP’s largest factory globally. For Matthias Lapp, CEO, LAPP Group, India’s importance goes beyond its size as a market. The country has become an important manufacturing, engineering and talent hub within the global LAPP network. “Celebrating 30 years is awesome. It feels great,” says Lapp. “India is our number one invested country from an Asia perspective.” He describes the country increasingly as a second home for LAPP. A Long-Term Bet on India LAPP’s decision to invest in India was driven by the opportunity to participate in a market where the industrial landscape was still developing. “There were opportunities, not everything was yet distributed and set in stone, so we could really participate in the growth, in the future growth,” Lapp recalls. content: ‘’A buyer asks for 500 pieces per style/Colour The factory merchandiser asks whether they meant 50,000 pcs’’ Somewhere between those two questions, an opportunity disappears. This small exchange captures a bigger challenge facing Bangladesh’s ready-made garment industry. The country has built a powerful business around producing large quantities efficiently. But the next generation of orders will require greater flexibility, stronger product development and dependable delivery. The question is changing from “How much can we produce?” to “How well can we respond?” The pressure is real. The picture is mixed. According to BGMEA’s published figures, Bangladesh exported $38.701 billion in garments in FY2025–26, down 1.64%** from the previous year. Garments still accounted for 80.62% of national merchandise export earnings. When the industry struggles, the effects reach workers, transport businesses, banks and households. Figure: Ruhul Talukder, Managing Director, Ruhrose RBT Ltd. London HQ, Bangladesh Manufacturing. However, the figures do not support the claim that buyers everywhere are leaving Bangladesh. EPB data reported by BSS and The Business Standard show garment exports to the EU fell 3.31% to $19.06 billion. Meanwhile, exports to the US increased 2.63% to $7.74 billion, and UK shipments rose 0.91% to $4.39 billion. These figures describe goods shipped, though. They cannot guarantee a healthy order book tomorrow. India, Vietnam and Pakistan remain serious competitors. Yet Bangladesh still attracts interest. In USFIA’s 2026 survey of 30 leading US fashion companies, 46.7% planned to increase sourcing from Bangladesh over the following two years. title: Weight-loss drugs help reshape apparel market
summary: The rapid adoption of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs is beginning to influence the fashion industry, changing clothing sizes, purchasing patterns and potentially the balance between online and physical retail. Drugs including Ozempic, Wegovy and Mounjaro are being associated with what has been dubbed the ‘Ozempic economy’, as significant changes in body weight encourage consumers to replace […] The post Weight-loss drugs help reshape apparel market appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: The rapid adoption of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs is beginning to influence the fashion industry, changing clothing sizes, purchasing patterns and potentially the balance between online and physical retail. Drugs including Ozempic, Wegovy and Mounjaro are being associated with what has been dubbed the ‘Ozempic economy’, as significant changes in body weight encourage consumers to replace clothing and reconsider what and how they buy. Research from PwC suggests the impact on apparel could be substantial. Some 73% of US GLP-1 users surveyed reported a meaningful change in clothing size, while apparel spending was 9.9% higher after users had been taking the drugs for six to eight months. The effects are also becoming apparent in the UK. PwC estimates that around three million British adults currently use GLP-1 medications, with 40% of users surveyed saying they were spending more on clothing. One consequence could be an unexpected revival in physical clothes shopping. A US survey of 500 GLP-1 users by returns management specialist ReturnPro found that 69% had become less confident about online sizing as their bodies changed, making the ability to try garments on in stores more important. Some 71% said they were buying more apparel as their size changed, while 58% reported increased spending on premium or higher-priced clothing. More than half expected their clothing expenditure to rise further once their weight had stabilised. The trend presents challenges as well as opportunities for retailers. ReturnPro found that 65% of GLP-1 consumers surveyed were buying several sizes of the same garment with the intention of returning those that did not fit, while 43% said their frequency of apparel returns had increased. content: Parkdale has acquired full ownership of CiCLO technology and plans to extend its use beyond apparel and home textiles into nonwovens, filtration, geotextiles and other technical applications. The Gastonia, North Carolina-based textile group has acquired the technology through its Parkdale Advanced Materials subsidiary, adding CiCLO to its growing portfolio of polymer and fibre technologies. CiCLO is a patented additive technology incorporated into polyester and nylon during fibre manufacture. It is designed to enable synthetic fibres that shed into the environment to biodegrade more readily in biologically active conditions, addressing the long-term persistence of microplastic fibres. The technology is already commercially used in apparel, home, hospitality and workwear products, but Parkdale sees considerable scope for expansion into markets where synthetic fibres are widely employed. These include industrial and hygiene nonwovens, geotextiles, filtration, insulation and furnishings. “We believe CiCLO fibres have the potential to address microplastic fibre persistence at meaningful scale,” said Davis Warlick, chief operating officer of Parkdale. “Our focus now is to continue investing in the technology, develop new applications with our customers, open new markets and broaden adoption.” CiCLO technology is incorporated into polyester and nylon at the polymer stage, creating pathways within the resulting fibres that allow naturally occurring microorganisms to break down the polymer in biologically active environments. title: Spider silk moves into major sportswear trial
title_ko: 스파이더 실크가 주요 스포츠웨어 시험에 진출
summary: Recombinant spider silk is moving a step closer to a commercial textile applications following the first customer shipment of yarn from US developer Kraig Biocraft Laboratories. The Ann Arbor, Michigan-based company has shipped a small quantity of custom-engineered spider silk yarn to an unnamed global performance sports brand, which plans to develop it into a […] The post Spider silk moves into major sportswear trial appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Recombinant spider silk is moving a step closer to a commercial textile applications following the first customer shipment of yarn from US developer Kraig Biocraft Laboratories. The Ann Arbor, Michigan-based company has shipped a small quantity of custom-engineered spider silk yarn to an unnamed global performance sports brand, which plans to develop it into a new performance textile. The order forms part of a confidential pilot development programme focused on high-performance athletic apparel. Kraig said the yarn had been processed to the customer’s specifications, although it has disclosed neither the identity of the brand nor the quantity supplied. The shipment is nevertheless significant for the company as its first commercial order for recombinant spider silk yarn and moves the technology beyond production development and into testing for an end-use textile application. Kraig produces its spider silk proteins using genetically engineered silkworms, an approach intended to combine some of the mechanical properties associated with natural spider silk with the established infrastructure and scalability of conventional silk production. Spider silk has long attracted interest from textile and materials developers because of its combination of strength, toughness, flexibility and low weight. Producing it economically and consistently at useful volumes, however, has proved considerably more difficult. Kraig believes specialist performance applications offer an appropriate starting point because relatively small quantities of material can potentially provide a meaningful performance benefit. “The volume is small by design,” said founder and CEO Kim Thompson. “This is a precision application, not a bulk order. summary: GREENSBORO, N.C.— September 30, 2026 — UNIFI, Inc., the makers of REPREVE® and one of the world’s innovators in recycled and synthetic yarns, today launches Cofira™, a versatile yarn that can be tailored with synthetic, blended, and functional fiber technologies for enhanced performance. This innovation within UNIFI®’s portfolio delivers a fusion of filament and spun […]
content: GREENSBORO, N.C.— September 30, 2026 — UNIFI, Inc., the makers of REPREVE® and one of the world’s innovators in recycled and synthetic yarns, today launches Cofira , a versatile yarn that can be tailored with synthetic, blended, and functional fiber technologies for enhanced performance. This innovation within UNIFI®’s portfolio delivers a fusion of filament and spun characteristics in one yarn, offering the advantage of spun yarn comfort with filament functionality. Cofira offers broad design flexibility that supports the integration of sustainable performance technologies. Designed for versatility, it is ideal for applications including apparel, furnishings, gear, and accessories. Key features of Cofira: Combines spun yarn aesthetics with filament yarn performance in one construction; Enables unique fabric aesthetics and hand feel; Can be combined with other UNIFI technologies including: A.M.Y. ® , ChillSense ® , and ReFlexx ® ; and Available globally in virgin and REPREVE polyester yarns, including REPREVE Takeback , with REPREVE options fully traceable via FiberPrint ® technology and certified by U-TRUST ® , GRS, and SCS for recycled content. In addition, UNIFI also announces the launch of Resist 2 O Pro, an expansion of water-resistant offerings engineered for all types of fabric formation. Designed to deliver durable water resistance without compromising fabric performance, Resist 2 O Pro gives brands and manufacturers greater freedom to develop water-resistant fabrics for a wide range of textile applications, without the use of topical treatments or fluorinated chemistry. content: “A Legacy of Excellence. A Future of Innovation.” BATEXPO 2026 is set to become one of the most significant platforms for showcasing the global capabilities, international credibility, and future potential of Bangladesh’s apparel industry. Returning after more than a decade, this mega event is more than just an exhibition—it represents an important national branding platform that will showcase the transformation of Bangladesh’s apparel sector, growing international buyer confidence, and its readiness for the future. Scheduled for 18–19 November 2026 at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Dhaka, BATEXPO 2026 is already generating significant international interest with the participation of leading global buyers, retailers, sourcing leaders, and fashion industry decision-makers. The involvement of globally recognised sourcing and supply-chain platform PDS Limited , along with senior representatives from international companies such as Primark, Pepco, M&S, Walmart Global Sourcing, Kmart, Cotton On, PDS, and LC Waikiki , sends a strong message about the growing confidence in Bangladesh as a strategic sourcing destination. A Decade of Transformation This confidence is not based solely on Bangladesh’s manufacturing capacity. It is the result of a remarkable transformation within the country’s apparel industry over the past decade. Significant progress has been made in workplace safety, workers’ wellbeing, social compliance, green manufacturing, resource efficiency, sustainability, digitalisation, automation, technology, product diversification, and higher-value manufacturing . title_ko: Rancon Lubricants, Invest Bangladesh의 국가 특별 경제 구역에서 6.5에이커에 대한 임대 계약 체결
summary: Rancon Lubricants Limited today signed a land lease agreement with Invest Bangladesh for 6.5 acres of developed land at the National Special Economic Zone in Mirsarai, Chattogram. The company proposes to invest USD 19.65 million in an industrial unit expected to create more than 250 jobs. Nahian Rahman Rochi, Member (Investment Development), signed on behalf […] The post Rancon Lubricants Signs Lease Agreement for 6.5 Acres at Invest Bangladesh’s National Special Economic Zone appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Rancon Lubricants Limited today signed a land lease agreement with Invest Bangladesh for 6.5 acres of developed land at the National Special Economic Zone in Mirsarai, Chattogram. The company proposes to invest USD 19.65 million in an industrial unit expected to create more than 250 jobs. Nahian Rahman Rochi, Member (Investment Development), signed on behalf of Invest Bangladesh, while Imran Zaman Khan, Managing Director, signed for Rancon Lubricants Limited. “This is Invest Bangladesh’s first land lease agreement following the merger of three investment promotion agencies,” said Nahian Rahman Rochi. “Commitments from anchor investors such as Rancon Lubricants signal confidence in the new institution and help build confidence among other investors,” he added. The lease runs for 50 years from the date of possession, with provision for renewal on terms set by Invest Bangladesh. Land handover is due within 90 days of signing. Rancon Lubricants is expected to begin construction within 120 days of handover and bring the unit into operation within 36 months of handover. Invest Bangladesh will facilitate utility connections and access to applicable government-declared customs duty, VAT and tax incentives. Rancon Lubricants will obtain the necessary approvals and comply with environmental, labour and safety requirements, including the provision of effluent and sewage treatment facilities and connection to the zone’s common effluent treatment and waste management systems. The agreement provides for performance and compliance monitoring, a period to remedy breaches before termination, and arbitration under the Arbitration Act, 2001. content: PARIS — October 5, 2026 — EverDye, the startup developing low-impact textile dyeing solutions, received two important recognition from the textile industry. The company secured the ZDHC Certification (Zero Discharge of Hazardous Chemicals), and is one of the 20 startups selected by CEMATEX (European Committee of Textile Machinery Manufacturers) for the CEMATEX Start-Up Grant. Founded in 2021, EverDye developed a bio-based pigment dyeing process that consumes less energy and operates at room temperature. This process reduces CO2 emissions by 90% and cuts energy consumption by 8 times compared to traditional textile dyeing methods. The company is led by Dr Amira Erokh, a materials chemist whose vision paved the way to a new approach. ZDHC certification: a labor for chemical management excellence ZDHC (Zero Discharge of Hazardous Chemicals) is a global initiative aiming to eliminate hazardous chemicals from the textile and leather industry. The certification attests to a chemical product’s compliance with the MRSL (Manufacturing Restricted Substances List), the list of substances prohibited or restricted during manufacturing. This mission resonates with EverDye, validating the technological approach of using bio-based pigments with the aim to limit chemical residues. “The ZDHC certification confirms that it is possible to transform the dyeing process without compromising on chemical control. At EverDye, we want to drive a profound shift in the industry toward a more responsible model, starting with dyeing.
